Existing systems address this challenge primarily through proxy representations or filter-and-rerank pipelines that reduce candidate generation to single-vector search. We study the complementary direction of building a native IVF-style index directly over multi-vector data. We introduce MV-IVF, an inverted-file index for multi-vector retrieval built on MV-Lloyd, a new Lloyd-style algorithm for clustering point clouds under a Chamfer objective. Our key observation is that once point clouds are assigned to clusters, the center-update step reduces to standard single-vector clustering over the flattened embeddings in each cluster. This enables efficient construction of a hierarchical IVF tree with center point clouds at internal nodes. At query time, MV-IVF performs best-first beam search over the tree to identify promising leaf clusters, then scores the documents in those leaves. We further accelerate search using low-bit quantization, query compression, and cache-efficient batched search. We implement MV-IVF in MVSIC, an optimized C++ library and unified evaluation framework for multi-vector retrieval that includes several major approaches. Across BEIR and LoTTE text retrieval benchmarks, MV-IVF achieves strong latency--recall tradeoffs, the best batched throughput frontiers, and favorable build-time and index-size profiles. At $90\%$ Recall-$10$@$10$, MV-IVF achieves up to $8.03\times$ lower single-query latency and up to $173.5\times$ higher QPS than the baselines, demonstrating that native IVF-style indexing is practical and effective for scalable multi-vector retrieval.

title: DobotTrack: Target-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Learning for Embodied Person Tracking
text: Title: DobotTrack: Target-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Learning for Embodied Person Tracking Shengjun Deng , Yinghan Zhang , Chengrui Wei , Liu Liang , Songyuan Liu , Pengkun Zheng , Yajun Zheng , Ying Zhang , Yuan Tian , Xi Li , Teng Wang Subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Language-guided embodied person tracking requires a mobile agent to identify a target from a referring description and consistently follow the target under egocentric observations. We present DobotTrack, a target-grounded vision-language-action (VLA) framework that integrates auxiliary grounding supervision with efficient temporal modeling. We systematically investigate five auxiliary tasks---person segmentation, bounding-box grounding, visual-spatial classification (VSC), future DINO feature prediction, and future-frame prediction---and adopt complementary mask and bounding-box supervision to enhance target delineation and localization. We introduce Q-identity, a target-conditioned historical visual compression module that leverages target-grounding predictions to selectively preserve identity-discriminative appearance features and spatial cues in compact historical tokens. On EVT-Bench, our 0.8B-parameter model achieves an average success rate of 77.9%, exceeding OmTrackVLA by 16.9 percentage points across the three tasks. We further construct a real-world person-tracking dataset collected using a quadruped robot, comprising 126 episodes and 596,323 mask-annotated frames. The target masks enable automatic derivation of bounding boxes and visual-spatial labels encoding horizontal position and apparent image scale, providing additional grounding supervision without separate manual annotation of these labels. Together, our framework and annotation pipeline support learning target-grounded tracking policies from simulated and real-world data. Code is available at this https URL .

title: Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection for Reasoning Distillation
text: Title: Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection for Reasoning Distillation Yijun Zhu , Jianxin Wang , Chengchao Shen Comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. The source code and trained weights are available at \url{ this https URL } Subjects: Computation and Language (cs.CL) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Machine Learning (cs.LG) Training smaller language models on reasoning solutions generated by a larger teacher model is the prevailing approach for transferring mathematical reasoning capabilities. However, the student tends to overfit the output distribution of the teacher and generalizes poorly when its own behavior at inference time deviates from the training data. Recent methods attempt to bridge this gap by incorporating error data, yet the corrective trajectories still reflect the reasoning patterns of the teacher, which the student cannot reliably reproduce, leaving the distribution mismatch largely unresolved. We propose a method, Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection (FPRT), built on the insight that effective training data should be jointly determined by what the student fails on and what it can realistically learn. Our method first profiles the failure behavior of the student on each problem through repeated sampling, characterizing it in terms of error rate and error consistency to reveal qualitatively distinct failure modes. Each mode demands a fundamentally different training signal. The diagnosed mode then guides candidate generation from the teacher via distinct prompting strategies tailored to each failure type. Among the correct candidates, our method selects the one whose initial reasoning steps after the point of divergence are most reproducible by the student. These first corrective steps constitute the primary bottleneck, while the remaining steps follow an already corrected context and can therefore be continued more readily. This contrasts with standard reranking approaches, which score the trajectory as a whole and thereby dilute the signal at the critical reasoning transition. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves the SOTA performance across the five benchmarks on both student backbones.

title: "Despite her age, Margaret was eager to make a change": Unpacking Aging Representations and Stereotypes in LLM-generated Stories
text: Title: "Despite her age, Margaret was eager to make a change": Unpacking Aging Representations and Stereotypes in LLM-generated Stories MD. Roqunuzzaman Sojib , Mohammad Sadat Hossain , Nafis Tahmid , Shattik Islam Rhythm , Novia Nurain Subjects: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC) As large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate everyday stories, their portrayals can shape expectations about aging. Prior work has largely examined age stereotypes in short responses, leaving unanswered whose lives models default to imagining and how age shapes characters' roles in complete narratives. We analyze 594 stories generated by Gemini, GPT, and Llama using text embeddings, LLM-assisted coding, and qualitative analysis. When age was unspecified, stories typically featured younger adults, with middle-aged protagonists largely absent. Older adults were often portrayed through loss, familiar routines, and help from younger characters. Even positive stories sometimes treated older adults' achievements as surprising or portrayed others making decisions on their behalf. We suggest evaluating not only the tone of generated stories, but also who appears, what opportunities they receive, and who makes decisions. Involving older adults in these evaluations can guide writing tools toward more varied, less stereotyped portrayals of later life.

title: When to Trust the BIM: Identifiability-Aware LiDAR-Inertial--BIM Fusion under As-Built Deviations
text: Title: When to Trust the BIM: Identifiability-Aware LiDAR-Inertial--BIM Fusion under As-Built Deviations Yujie Zhang , Yuxuan Guo , Xinbao Sun , Chunlei Zhao , Langqi Miao , Xiaohui Jia , Jinyue Liu Comments: 24 pages, 12 figures, 11 tables (including appendices) Subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) Building information models (BIM) can provide a global geometric reference for robot localization with LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO). However, as-built deviations from the as-designed model mean that a disagreement between a scan and the BIM may arise from a pose error, an offset wall surface (an as-built deviation or an unmodeled object in front of the wall), or a shifted room, and in some geometries these explanations produce identical observations. In this paper, we formalize this attribution problem as fault identification over three fault classes and derive a geometric criterion for when attribution is possible. Building on it, we propose an identifiability-aware method that reports an attribution only when the fault is attributable; otherwise, it retains the candidates, defers BIM updates and BIM-based pose corrections in the ambiguous directions, and recovers once new references arrive. In the pre-registered two-dimensional study, on cases whose fault is detectable but not attributable, the method's conditional error rate was 0.83%, against 31.67% for a baseline with uncertainty-based abstention at the same answer rate. On the 5,600 attributable cases, the method reported a unique attribution 5,574 times, with no incorrect attributions. In paired fault injections in a laboratory room with its IFC model and on three floors of the SLABIM dataset, it raised no off-target attribution (0 of 168 conditions in the laboratory; 0 of 1,302 on SLABIM) and attributed all eight laboratory faults predicted to be attributable, whereas both reproduced baselines raised off-target structural flags in every setting.

title: When Can You Trust Neural Critics? Auditing Mutual Information Estimates of Higher-Order Epistasis in Protein Language Models
text: Title: When Can You Trust Neural Critics? Auditing Mutual Information Estimates of Higher-Order Epistasis in Protein Language Models Maryam Rahimimovassagh , Waldemar Karwowski , Niloofar Yousefi Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) Mutual information (MI) estimation is used to probe what neural representations encode, including in protein language models, but variational MI estimators have variance that scales at least exponentially in the true MI. We audit a prior neural-MI study of order-resolved epistasis in ESM-2 on the four-site GB1 landscape. Run-to-run differences show no systematic bias and a magnitude comparable to ordinary cross-seed retraining variability, and the evaluation-pairing scheme shifts scores substantially. At the original dimensionality, two of three alternative estimator families stabilize the estimate across seeds and one does not. In a synthetic calibration at the representation dimensionalities of two other protein language models (a Gaussian channel with known MI; no model representations), all three families recover materially less signal than required, despite correct signal ordering and stable seeds. A control critic given the true signal direction, which also reduces its input to one dimension, recovers 93.3% and 98.7% of the analytic MI at gain 1.5 (at 5,120 and 4,096 dimensions), so the signal is recoverable with privileged information, but the control does not identify why blind estimation fails. We package the checks into a reusable diagnostic protocol and conclude that even a stabilized estimator is not currently sufficient for order-resolved dependence claims made under blind search at this dimensionality and sample size.

title: Grounding-Aware Judge Reward Reinforcement Learning for Out-of-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing
text: Title: Grounding-Aware Judge Reward Reinforcement Learning for Out-of-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing Xiaoyong Yu , Xinge Yu Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) must distinguish genuine faces from presentation attacks. A unified Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) is an attractive solution: it detects physical attacks (print, replay, mask) in one model and produces interpretable forensic evidence via Chain-of-Thought (CoT). A central obstacle to post-training such a model with reinforcement learning is that FAS reasoning has no rule-verifiable ground truth: only the binary verdict is checkable, while the reasoning chain cannot be verified by any hand-crafted rule. Optimizing the verdict alone is therefore a sparse, hackable signal. The model can reach the correct answer through a shortcut such as a false-rejection bias, which does not generalize. We address this with a grounding-aware judge reward. A 32B vision-language judge scores each reasoning chain against the image on evidence anchoring, logical coherence, and domain knowledge, turning the image itself into the verification signal. The reward is applied in a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) stage after CoT supervised fine-tuning. It is the judge, rather than the RL objective, that supplies the process supervision a verdict-only reward cannot. Our study starts from a model that already performs well In-Domain (ID) after CoT-based supervised fine-tuning and asks how to improve its Out-of-Domain (OOD) generalization. We find that grounding-aware rewards are an effective means to that end. We validate the method on OOD generalization, where the reward reduces ACER on two physical benchmarks (LCC-FASD 0.288 to 0.273, MSU-MFSD 0.431 to 0.409) while preserving ID accuracy (CelebA-Spoof 0.033 to 0.035). Against ResNet-50/101 and CLIP-ViT-B/16 baselines, the MLLM dominates ID and matches or surpasses the strongest baseline OOD. To our knowledge this is the first use of LLM-as-judge process supervision for FAS.

title: LeanDojo-v2: A Comprehensive Library for AI-Assisted Theorem Proving in Lean
text: Title: LeanDojo-v2: A Comprehensive Library for AI-Assisted Theorem Proving in Lean Ryan Hsiang , William Adkisson , Robert Joseph George , Anima Anandkumar Comments: 11 pages, 7 figures, accepted to NeurIPS Math-AI workshop Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) Building on recent progress in machine learning for formal theorem proving in Lean, we introduce LeanDojo-v2: an end-to-end framework that unifies repository data extraction, LLM fine-tuning, proof search, AI autocompletion, and LLM-assisted theorem proving in a single software library. In addition, we provide Lean4Code, a lightweight IDE that integrates the various features of LeanDojo-v2 through a simple, mathematician-friendly UI. These tools will enable mathematicians and researchers to easily fine-tune language models on domain-specific Lean codebases and experiment with LLM-assisted theorem proving without a complex setup.

title: StreamTab: Training-Free Temporal Link Prediction with Tabular Foundation Models
text: Title: StreamTab: Training-Free Temporal Link Prediction with Tabular Foundation Models Mingqi Yang , Renqi Wu Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Databases (cs.DB); Social and Information Networks (cs.SI) Temporal link prediction uses past interactions to predict whether two nodes will interact in the future. Temporal graph neural networks achieve strong results on this task, but they are trained separately for each graph. How a model should use interaction history also depends on the candidates it is compared with. A past interaction can distinguish a recurring link from a random pair that has never interacted, but when the negative candidates have also interacted before, other signals are needed. We propose StreamTab, a training-free framework built on a frozen tabular foundation model pretrained only on synthetic tables. StreamTab describes each candidate pair by statistics of its past interactions and shows the model recent observed interactions and sampled negative pairs as labeled examples, from which the model scores new candidates. Its central design, regime conditioning, samples the negative examples according to how the candidates are sampled, so the examples show the distinction the model must make. As new interactions arrive, StreamTab updates the statistics and refreshes the examples while the model parameters stay fixed. On thirteen datasets against 21 temporal graph baselines, StreamTab achieves the highest average precision on twelve datasets under historical sampling and eleven under inductive sampling, and ranks first or stays within one point of the best on seven datasets under random sampling. With the same features and model, regime conditioning raises average precision over examples with random negatives by a median of 12.6 points under historical sampling.

title: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
text: Title: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations Tianchi Yu , Ivan Oseledets Subjects: Numerical Analysis (math.NA) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Machine Learning (cs.LG) Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.

title: From Emergence to Reversibility: Toward Reversible Multi-Agent Systems
text: Title: From Emergence to Reversibility: Toward Reversible Multi-Agent Systems Zhengye Han , Linda Ng Boyle Subjects: Multiagent Systems (cs.MA) Multi-agent systems become capable through institutional mechanisms, such as rules that route information to agents that act on it. These mechanisms are also natural places to restrict the system. Yet as agents learn, share memory, delegate, and repair failures, the collective can find other paths to the same effects: a restriction on the original mechanism still operates but no longer stops them, while routine performance and compliance checks pass. We propose \textbf{Reversible Multi-agent Systems} as a research agenda: collectives that grow while an authorized supervisor can still restrict specified effects, keep them restricted as agents adapt, and reconstitute useful cooperation under renewed authority. What is reversed is the ability to produce a specified effect; restrictions must hold even if learned knowledge persists. The goal is to preserve effective intervention, not a particular mechanism: at every step of growth, some authorized intervention must keep a specified prohibited effect rare while maintaining required service. We identify three research problems: tracking what capabilities depend on, handing off control before an old mechanism loses its effect, and separating legitimate repair from unauthorized reconstruction. We outline how to evaluate control across growth paths, back control claims with evidence, and allocate the rights to restrict and restore.

title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
text: Title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling Yunhan Yang , Yunfei Zhao , Zeqiang Lai , Jiachen Xu , Minxiu Wang , Xintong Han , Xiangyu Yue , Xihui Liu , Chunchao Guo Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns a shared latent space that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs, allowing data-rich geometric and visual priors to support data-scarce part learning. Given a single input image, the base model generates geometry, deformation, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset without a separate segmentation stage. We further tune the pretrained model for two extensions: a point-prompt adapter that maps arbitrary 3D point prompts with binary part IDs into latent tokens for full segmentation, refinement, and part subdivision, and an amodal part completion model that completes partial surface masks into a coherent full-object decomposition through dynamic per-part token allocation, cross-attention to the given geometry latent, and alternating part-local and global attention. Extensive experiments show that OmniLatent produces semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, supports interactive part editing, and completes partial part observations while preserving global object consistency.

title: Real-Time Short-Response Selection for Spoken Dialogue Systems
text: Title: Real-Time Short-Response Selection for Spoken Dialogue Systems Hien Ohnaka , Kazuyo Onishi , Koichiro Yoshino Comments: 10 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables Subjects: Sound (cs.SD) ; Computation and Language (cs.CL) To realize spoken dialogue systems that can interact naturally with users, it is important for the system to respond to user utterances at appropriate timings. To achieve such natural turn-taking, the system needs not only to predict appropriate response timings but also to mask delays caused by language generation and speech synthesis so that they are not perceived by the user. We propose a real-time short-response selection task that can be integrated with existing turn-taking models to mask generation delay. To address this task, the proposed model learns the mapping between dialogue context and short responses using contrastive learning. When a turn-taking event is detected, the system selects a response from a set of pre-generated candidates. The selected response is played while the main response is being generated. Experimental results show that the proposed method learns to select short responses based on dialogue context, outperforming random and LLM-based baselines. Moreover, integrating response selection maintained turn-taking prediction performance and added minimal processing overhead.

title: ProtoCouncil: Multi-Encoder Anatomical Prototypes for Prostate Cancer Detection in Micro-Ultrasound
text: Title: ProtoCouncil: Multi-Encoder Anatomical Prototypes for Prostate Cancer Detection in Micro-Ultrasound Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi , Nooshin Maghsoodi , Armin Saadat , Obed Dzikunu , Zhuoxin Guo , Hannes Cash , Ferdinand Luger , Adam Kinnaird , Brian Wodlinger , Parvin Mousavi , Purang Abolmaesumi Comments: 12 pages, 3 figures, Under Review Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Machine Learning (cs.LG) Purpose: Micro-ultrasound ($\mu$US) is a promising modality for prostate cancer (PCa) detection, but identifying suspicious tissue depends heavily on clinical experience. Models trained on sparse, noisy core-level pathology offer little insight into their decisions and can fail under domain shift. Clinical use needs a traceable decision process and a flag for uncertain predictions. Methods: We introduce ProtoCouncil, in which three foundation encoders (MedSAM, DINOv3 and V-JEPA 2.1) learn case-based prototypes at three anatomical levels: whole gland, needle track and gland sectors. Prototypes are projected onto real training-core regions, and label-free fusion keeps every class logit as a bias plus an exact sum of prototype similarity contributions. Encoder disagreement triggers selective prediction. Results: In five-fold patient-level cross-validation (6,588 cores, 693 patients), ProtoCouncil reaches 82.9% AUROC for clinically significant PCa (csPCa, Grade Group $\geq$3), 4.3 points above the best previously published method. In zero-shot evaluation on two external cohorts, ProtoCouncil achieves higher all-cancer and csPCa AUROC than all previous methods. Nearest same-class exemplars match test-core tumor involvement better than random same-class cases. Externally, csPCa accuracy falls from 79% when encoders agree to 27% when two oppose the fused call. Abstaining on disagreement raises balanced accuracy by 7 and 15 points, while retaining 58% and 54% of the cores. Conclusion: ProtoCouncil grounds core-level predictions in exact similarity-based evidence from real, anatomically indexed training cases, which makes its reasoning interpretable. It achieves the highest csPCa AUROC across three cohorts and identifies unreliable predictions through encoder disagreement.

title: Robust Readout of Cross-Point Resistive Arrays via Time-Domain Optimization
text: Title: Robust Readout of Cross-Point Resistive Arrays via Time-Domain Optimization Taro Tako , Hiroshi Kaminaga , Taisuke Kobayashi Comments: 4 pages, 1 figure, IEEE Sensors 2026 accepted Subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) Cross-point resistive arrays are attractive for high-density tactile sensing because they reduce wiring complexity. However, conventional frequency-based readout methods can become inaccurate in robotic sensing environments, where long interconnects and measurement and environmental noise degrade the observed signals. We propose a time-domain optimization method for robust readout of cross-point resistive arrays. The method determines resistance values by fitting a time-domain observation model to the measured waveform over the interval, rather than relying solely on spectral amplitudes. By exploiting the full waveform, the proposed method improves robustness under noisy observation conditions. In simulations of a 16 x 16 array, the proposed method reduced the mean readout error by 20% compared with the baseline method. Furthermore, validation over 1,000 trials showed that the proposed method achieves more robust estimation than the conventional method, reducing the mean error and standard deviation by 24.6% and 77.6%, respectively. The improvement was also confirmed in cross-point array simulations with resistance distributions emulating tactile sensor responses.

title: Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
text: Title: Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective Sophie Hall , Heinrich H. Nax , Saverio Bolognani Comments: Book chapter, 25 pages, 4 figures. To appear in Socio-Inspired and Socially Aware Control for Complex Systems, Springer Subjects: Computer Science and Game Theory (cs.GT) ; Systems and Control (eess.SY); Optimization and Control (math.OC) Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.

title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models?
text: Title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models? Ruichen Zheng , Yihe Wang , Fabrice Harel-Canada , Sara Khosravi , Zeynep Senahan Yildiz , Amit Sahai , Nanyun Peng Subjects: Computation and Language (cs.CL) Benchmark gains from reasoning-enhanced large language models encourage the assumption that these models should broadly perform better on complex generative tasks, but this remains underexplored in open-ended, creative domains shaped by nuances of reader experience. We tested this assumption through the lens of psychological depth in short stories. We compared DeepSeek-R1 vs. DeepSeek-V3, our closest available contrast for reasoning-oriented post-training, and GPT-5 vs. GPT-4o, through 60 blinded pairwise evaluations in which seven human annotators and an ensemble LLM-as-a-Judge rated prompt-matched story outputs. Human evaluations showed no universal reasoning advantage: GPT-5 was slightly preferred over GPT-4o (60.0-62.9% across two reasoning-effort settings), whereas DeepSeek-R1 fell behind DeepSeek-V3 (42.9%). Although this pattern was marked by low inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's $\alpha = 0.070$), our annotation-quality checks suggested genuine evaluative subjectivity, plausibly reflecting distinct annotator decision schemes rather than annotation failure. In contrast, the LLM-as-a-Judge showed a strong pro-reasoning bias (98.3% of pairs vs. 55.2% of human votes), consistent across its five configurations and partly tracking sentence length. These findings suggest that, at the frontier, reasoning-related quality differences are small enough to be dominated by reader subjectivity, and that LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators can obscure this subjectivity in nuanced creative-generation tasks.

title: MongoBench: Do LLMs Know What a MongoDB Query Will Do?
text: Title: MongoBench: Do LLMs Know What a MongoDB Query Will Do? Qibai Chen , Haoting Qiu , Yezhou Cheng , Mengxiao Qian Comments: Accepted at CAIT 2026 Subjects: Software Engineering (cs.SE) ; Databases (cs.DB) LLM agents increasingly operate databases on their own: they generate queries and run them against live data. Two checks are commonly used to judge such an agent - whether it produces a valid query, and whether it reaches the right final answer - but neither tells us whether the agent knows what its query will actually do before it runs. We argue that this consequence prediction ability must be evaluated in its own right, and we build MongoBench to measure it: given a collection of documents and a MongoDB find() filter, a model must return the exact set of matching _ids, with ground truth from a real mongod server. The 300 items each compose three or four documented matching pitfalls and are proposed symmetrically by three vendors' models, so results stratify by item source. Evaluating four models - frontier systems from three vendors and one open-weight reasoner - accuracy ranges from 70.1% to 92.1%, a 22-point spread. Each proposer mispredicts 10-31% of the items it wrote itself, so producing a query does not imply predicting its effect. A failure-mode analysis shows errors are better predicted by which semantic pitfall a query exercises - range comparisons and null - than by surface measures such as document count or the number of composed rules. Prepending a verified rule sheet helps unevenly; executing the original filter against the engine yields reliable match sets, but delegation must be checked: on 28% of items (averaged over three runs) one model's executed filters never passed a canonical check against the intended query, and it answered about 22 of them wrong, while the other three passed on every item. We release the benchmark, the mongod oracle, and the evaluation code with all prompts at this https URL .

title: WearableBridge: Task-Guided Latent Transport for Free-Living Activity Recognition
text: Title: WearableBridge: Task-Guided Latent Transport for Free-Living Activity Recognition Jingjing Zou , Yixin Wang Comments: 26 pages, 5 figures, 11 tables. Code and interactive demo: this https URL Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) Wrist-worn accelerometers make activity monitoring feasible at scale, but incidental arm motion, device orientation, and shifting context blur the signal that separates activities. Calibration studies supply higher-quality references such as concurrent thigh recordings or supervised laboratory wrist sessions, but they are expensive, cover few participants, and are rarely available at deployment. How can limited reference data improve recognition for participants who wear only a wrist device? We propose WearableBridge, which holds the reference encoder and classifier fixed and learns a task-guided transport map, the bridge, that carries each wrist feature into the region the classifier associates with its activity. Reference features or the classifier's predictions indicate the destination, and a classification loss penalizes wrist features that land in the region of another activity. We instantiate WearableBridge with three bridges: Mapper regresses onto reference features, Distillation matches the classifier's class probabilities, and MeanFlow learns a one-step flow from wrist toward reference features. On 40 held-out free-living PAAWS participants, all three bridges improve macro-F1 in every training run, and the strongest, MeanFlow, raises mean macro-F1 from 35.1% to 56.0% with concurrent thigh references (Thigh2Wrist), and from 54.0% to 63.5% with group-matched laboratory wrist references (Lab2Freeliving). Fitted only on PAAWS, MeanFlow also raises macro-F1 on the CAPTURE-24 cohort from 42.8% to 54.7%. The gains replicate on selfBACK, hold across four reference encoders, and grow with temporal context. A study can therefore collect reference recordings for a calibration subset and improve wrist-only recognition for every other participant, training only a bridge of 0.13 to 2.44 million parameters while the reference encoder and classifier stay unchanged.

title: UniRGBA: Unifying RGB and Alpha in Pretrained Video Diffusion Models
text: Title: UniRGBA: Unifying RGB and Alpha in Pretrained Video Diffusion Models Lei Xu , Zhuo Li , Yongyi Jin , Aoyu Wang Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) Recent advances in video diffusion models have achieved remarkable photorealistic RGB synthesis, yet generating videos with a native alpha channel remains an open challenge. Existing approaches often rely on matting-style data and non-native RGBA designs, causing them to specialize in real-object scenes and to degrade severely on visual-effect content whose semi-transparency is spatially non-local and non-elliptical. We present UniRGBA, a unified framework whose key insight is that RGBA generation does not require a dedicated alpha encoder or complex latent-space restructuring---a minimal, targeted extension of the existing RGB pathway is sufficient. UniRGBA-VAE extends a causal video VAE to 4-channel RGBA via zero-initialized channel expansion, symmetric selective layer unfreezing (5% trainable), and a six-term progressive reconstruction loss anchored by a KL reference loss that prevents latent drift, followed by a two-stage schedule that introduces a lightweight GAN objective. We then apply standard DoRA to the pretrained DiT, reusing the unified 4-channel latent without any alpha-specific architectural changes. On a visual-effect RGBA benchmark, UniRGBA substantially outperforms Wan-Alpha on RGBA reconstruction while preserving RGB fidelity. For generation, UniRGBA outperforms Wan-Alpha on RGBA text-to-video tasks and matches or surpasses the original pretrained Wan2.1 backbone on RGB-only metrics, demonstrating that native alpha support can be integrated without compromising the underlying RGB prior or the model's architectural versatility.

title: Vertex Deletion on $H$-Induced-Minor-Free Graphs: Subexponential FPT Algorithms and Approximation Schemes
text: Title: Vertex Deletion on $H$-Induced-Minor-Free Graphs: Subexponential FPT Algorithms and Approximation Schemes Daniel Lokshtanov , Fahad Panolan , Saket Saurabh , Jie Xue , Meirav Zehavi Subjects: Data Structures and Algorithms (cs.DS) ; Discrete Mathematics (cs.DM) We study vertex-deletion problems on string graphs and, more generally, on graphs excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor. For every fixed graph $H$, fixed nonnegative integer $t$, and fixed monadic second-order formula $\phi$, we consider the problem of finding a minimum-cardinality set $S$ such that $G-S$ has treewidth at most $t$ and satisfies $\phi$. This captures classic problems such as Vertex Cover, Feedback Vertex Set, and deletion to graphs of any fixed bounded treewidth. We give an algorithm with running time $2^{k^{2/3} \log^{O(1)} k}n^{O(1)}$ on $H$-induced-minor-free graphs, where $k$ is the optimum deletion-set size. This resolves in the affirmative the open problem highlighted by Bonnet and Rzążewski [Algorithmica 2019] and Berthe, Bougeret, Gonçalves, and Raymond [ICALP 2025] regarding the existence of a subexponential parameterized algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on string graphs. Our algorithm significantly improves over existing parameterized algorithms for more restricted classes of problems on more restricted classes of graphs. When the property defined by $\phi$ is hereditary, we also obtain a quasi-polynomial time approximation scheme, namely an algorithm that produces a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution in quasi-polynomial time. Both the sub-exponential algorithm and the quasi-polynomial time approximation scheme build on the same new structural and algorithmic insights.

title: Emo-LiveSync: Real-Time Universal Lip Synchronization with Explicit Emotion Control
text: Title: Emo-LiveSync: Real-Time Universal Lip Synchronization with Explicit Emotion Control Sangjoon Yu , Seungeun Lee , JoonHeyok Shin , Ji-Su Kang Comments: Accepted to BMVC 2026, 23 pages, 16 figures Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Lip synchronization, the task of generating realistic lip movements synchronized with audio signals, is fundamental to applications such as film dubbing, virtual avatars, and digital content creation. Recent GAN-based methods offer computational efficiency but often lack visual fidelity, while diffusion-based approaches achieve high-quality results at the cost of substantial computational overhead. Moreover, most existing methods are limited to photo-realistic human faces, restricting their applicability to stylized characters and non-human entities. In this paper, we propose an efficient universal lip-sync video generation framework that achieves high-quality results without compromising computational efficiency. We build on LivePortrait, a warp-based portrait animation model, and introduce a training strategy that aligns audio signals to an implicit motion space by distilling knowledge from a pre-trained video-to-motion model. This enables real-time inference while maintaining high visual fidelity, and naturally generalizes to diverse stylistic characters beyond photo-realistic humans. Furthermore, we introduce an expressive control gate that enables explicit manipulation of emotional expressions for content enrichment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both visual quality and lip-sync accuracy while ensuring real-time inference.

title: Large Language Model Deployment on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices: A Practitioners Survey
text: Title: Large Language Model Deployment on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices: A Practitioners Survey Rahul Maliakkal , Yashasvi Makin , Plawan Rath , Rohit Jain , Ankur Sadhoo Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL) Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed many areas of artificial intelligence (AI), but their substantial resource requirements limit their deployment on mobile and edge devices. Although LLMs have demonstrated impressive capabilities in various applications, the next challenge is deploying these models on resource-limited edge devices. Recent innovations in software optimizations and specialized hardware have made it feasible to deploy LLMs on edge devices. Edge deployment offers benefits including local data processing, cost savings, reduced latency, and personalized responses. This paper reviews the latest techniques that make the deployment of LLMs on edge devices feasible.

title: GlobalPuzzle: Globally Informed Genetic Search for Eroded Jigsaw Puzzle Reassembly
text: Title: GlobalPuzzle: Globally Informed Genetic Search for Eroded Jigsaw Puzzle Reassembly Lunyan Wang , Chuanzhi Xu , Ziyuan Tao , Weidong Cai Comments: 22 pages (10 pages main paper and 12 pages supplementary material), 16 figures Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) Jigsaw puzzle reassembly remains a highly challenging task, particularly when piece boundaries are irregularly eroded to simulate damage to cultural artifacts. On the GAP benchmark, existing methods achieve a perfect assembly accuracy of only 0.3% on $5 \times 5$ puzzles, whereas humans can solve jigsaw puzzles with remarkably high accuracy. Humans typically approach puzzle solving by identifying potentially adjacent pieces, evaluating the current assembly, and iteratively performing complex operations such as adding pieces, replacing incorrectly placed pieces, and moving entire connected groups of pieces. However, existing methods face a fundamental limitation: approaches that leverage global visual information typically predict piece arrangements directly, making it difficult to explicitly perform such complex iterative operations, while search based methods can rearrange pieces but primarily rely on pairwise boundary compatibility, lacking global visual information to evaluate and guide the search process. To bridge this gap, we propose GlobalPuzzle, a jigsaw puzzle reassembly framework that integrates global canvas level evaluation, action guidance, and genetic search. By incorporating global visual information into the evaluation and optimization of candidate assemblies, GlobalPuzzle aims to resolve ambiguous adjacency relationships that are difficult to determine from irregularly eroded piece boundaries alone, enabling flexible, globally informed reconstruction.

title: BrainCoT: A Multi-Task Zero-Shot Brain Signal Foundation Model with Neurometric-Anchored Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
text: Title: BrainCoT: A Multi-Task Zero-Shot Brain Signal Foundation Model with Neurometric-Anchored Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Yiyu Gui , Mingzhi Chen , Guibo Luo , Yuchao Yang Comments: 37 pages. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) Brain signals exhibit substantial multi-center heterogeneity, strong inter-subject variability, and highly diverse task settings, which makes it difficult to build models that generalize beyond a single task. While recent brain signal foundation models leverage large-scale pretraining to learn generalizable representations, they often fall short in practice because they still require target-data-specific supervised adaptation, lack multi-task zero-shot capability, and rarely provide verifiable evidence to support their predictions. In this work, we present BrainCoT, a multi-task zero-shot Brain signal foundation model with neurometric-anchored Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. BrainCoT unifies heterogeneous tasks into an instruction-driven framework so that, after pretraining, a single model can be directly applied to multiple tasks in zero-shot settings without additional adaptation. It further introduces neurometric-anchored chain-of-thought grounded in neurometric evidence for verifiable reasoning, and adopts Decision-Consistent Rationale Training to keep process learning aligned with correct predictions. Across extensive evaluations, BrainCoT achieves an average ACC of 67.41% and AUC of 74.33% in zero-shot classification without downstream training data, outperforming the strongest linear-probing baseline trained with 1% labeled downstream data by 3.85% in ACC and 5.97% in AUC.

title: Training-Free Active Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
text: Title: Training-Free Active Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models Jihwan Bang , Sumyeong Ahn , Hwanjun Song , Jae-Gil Lee Comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) Test-time adaptation (TTA) for vision-language models (VLMs) is usually studied in a fully unsupervised regime, where adaptation relies on pseudo-labels, confidence scores, or entropy computed by the model itself. This is a severe restriction on hard shifted samples: the model is asked to repair its own uncertain predictions without any external evidence. At the other extreme, supervised online adaptation assumes labels can directly train or correct the model. We study the intermediate deployment regime between these two extremes. In Active Test-time Adaptation for VLMs (Active VLM-TTA), a pretrained VLM may spend an explicit labeling budget on selected test samples, but the prediction for the current sample must be emitted before its label can be used; queried labels are therefore costed, delayed evidence for future samples rather than free correction for the present one. Under this future-only constraint, the central question is how to reuse sparse labels conservatively. We instantiate this setting with ACTive VLM-TTA for Online Retrieval (ACTOR), a training-free plug-in module that routes uncertain samples among base prediction, label query, and memory-based correction using a consistency-and-reliability check over previously queried labels. Across ten cross-domain benchmarks and a domain-transfer benchmark based on ImageNet, ACTOR consistently improves strong VLM-TTA baselines on ResNet and ViT backbones with negligible inference overhead. Our implementation is publicly available at this https URL .

title: The Invisible Gap: Romanized Indic Generation Fails Where Automatic Metrics Succeed
text: Title: The Invisible Gap: Romanized Indic Generation Fails Where Automatic Metrics Succeed Madhu Sudhan Rao Beesetty , Surbhi Sharma , Devesh Maheshwari , Lokesh Meesala Comments: 11 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables. All authors contributed equally Subjects: Computation and Language (cs.CL) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) Hundreds of millions of Indians communicate with digital systems in romanized Latin characters -- typing "aap kaise hain" rather than native script -- yet romanized Indic generation is absent from NLP benchmarks and evaluation frameworks. We demonstrate that automatic metrics (BGE-M3, BERTScore) systematically misrepresent the quality of romanized Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada generation. We evaluate four LLMs (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 2.5-flash, Qwen3.5-35B) on 142 OpenAssistant query-response pairs. On a 72-response diagnostic subset, native speakers rate GPT-5.5 1.43 points higher than Claude Opus 4.8 on a 12-point rubric, whereas their full-dataset BGE-M3 means differ by only 0.004. Two distinct model-specific failure modes emerge: Gemini produces script spillage (16.9% of Telugu responses leak native script), while Qwen collapses to English-only output (16.2% of Kannada responses). We introduce a failure-aware evaluation policy that assigns zero to empty outputs, script-corrupted responses, and instruction collapses -- revealing failures metrics alone cannot detect. Our results show that evaluating romanized Indic generation requires a coordinated bundle: semantic similarity, script compliance, failure coverage, and native-speaker acceptability.

title: When Routine Operations Break Architectural Pattern Relationships in LLM Agent Harnesses
text: Title: When Routine Operations Break Architectural Pattern Relationships in LLM Agent Harnesses Boming Xia , Qinghua Lu , Dino Sejdinovic , Liming Zhu Subjects: Software Engineering (cs.SE) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) LLM agent harnesses distribute tool mediation, state management and safety guardrails across native services, independently written plugins and configuration. Routine operations can change the runtime order or retained state that architectural pattern relationships require, without any code change. We study five relationships associated with the Guardrail Enforcement Point, Autonomy Controller and Blackboard patterns across five released harnesses, analysing a main sample of fourteen independently written plugins. Using PatternOps, our assessment procedure, we trace requirements from pattern descriptions, provider documentation and deployment profiles to the providers that realise them and the records that decide them. We then compare alternative allocations under supported operations. Such operations broke relationships silently: after a plugin was reapplied or an allow rule saved, policy stopped evaluating edits while every plugin stayed active, and a prohibited edit executed. Which alternatives qualified depended on the requirement. Allocations that kept the required order, or kept or rebuilt the needed state, held on their tested paths and operation sequences, while others prevented prohibited effects but missed edits rejected elsewhere. In these harnesses, a pattern relationship is a property of the running system and its history, so architects should evaluate it against the decision paths, state lifetimes and operation sequences their deployments use.

title: EventHOI: Event-Driven Resource-Efficient Hand-Object Interaction Logging on Smartglasses
text: Title: EventHOI: Event-Driven Resource-Efficient Hand-Object Interaction Logging on Smartglasses Le Zhang , Kailai Cui , Hao Chen , Vlad Roznyatovskiy , Jianzhong Zhang , Anhong Guo , Kang G. Shin , Ke Sun Comments: 15 pages, 21 figures, 3 tables Subjects: Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing (cs.DC) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC) Hand-object interactions (HOIs) can be captured by smartglasses to learn how people manipulate objects in daily life. Automatic logging of these interactions from an egocentric perspective provides time-stamped evidence of daily actions for applications like memory assistance. However, continuous RGB capture and wireless transmission exceed the energy and bandwidth budgets of smartglasses. We present EventHOI, an event-driven sensing and compression system that couples selective RGB capture with HOI-aware encoding to enable egocentric logging over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) while preserving downstream HOI logging performance. Our key insight is to use low-power event sensing both to determine when RGB capture is needed and to identify where visual detail must be preserved. A lightweight IMU-based egomotion cancellation pipeline suppresses egomotion-induced events so that residual HOI motion can guide RGB triggering and spatial compression. We build a smartglasses prototype and conduct an end-to-end evaluation of EventHOI on a 50-hour egocentric benchmark with 97 subjects and a 20-hour real-world dataset we collect from 10 participants, together covering a broad range of daily-life scenarios and environments. Compared to RGB-only baselines, EventHOI reduces always-on backend power consumption by 5.8-10.4x and uplink bandwidth by 2.9x, with minimal HOI recognition accuracy loss. The resulting RGB uplink of less than 130 kbps fits within commodity BLE bandwidth budgets, making stable BLE video streaming feasible for egocentric HOI logging. Demo video and project website: this https URL

title: MARS: Training Multilingual Search Agents for Retriever-Free Evidence Acquisition
text: Title: MARS: Training Multilingual Search Agents for Retriever-Free Evidence Acquisition Rui Qi , Yunlong Liang , Yufeng Chen , Jinan Xu , Fandong Meng , Kaiyu Huang Subjects: Computation and Language (cs.CL) Existing multilingual retrieval-augmented generation relies heavily on learned retrievers and similarity-based ranking from multilingual collections, which are vulnerable to cross-lingual retrieval errors and indexing overhead. In this paper, we explore retriever-free multilingual search, where the model directly interacts with raw corpora through executable shell commands. This paradigm shifts the bottleneck to multilingual search action generation, where exact search is sensitive to entity surface forms and outcome-only supervision provides limited guidance for multi-turn search. To address these challenges, we propose MARS, a multilingual search agent in direct corpus interaction (DCI) with reinforcement learning (RL). MARS introduces corpus-native entity grounding to recover reliable lexical anchors from corpus evidence, mitigating failure to retrieve evidence. Meanwhile, we present a redundancy-aware search reward to encourage concise and effective search trajectories, addressing training collapse in RL of multilingual scenarios. Experiments show that \ours~consistently outperforms strong retrieval-based and DCI baselines, while demonstrating robust cross-lingual generalization and substantially reducing redundant corpus interactions.

title: TUGB: A Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding Framework
text: Title: TUGB: A Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding Framework Luzhan Yuan , Chao Mi , Xiahao Shi , Yi Mao , Shengsheng Niu , Xin Zhu , Jie He , Zhangang Lin , Ching Law Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) Generative modeling, particularly Decision Transformers, shows promise in auto-bidding strategies. However, it struggles with limited exploration in static offline datasets, vulnerability to dynamic environmental shifts, and a reliance on heuristic return-to-go (RTG) specifications that may yield suboptimal performance on unseen traffic. To address these challenges, we propose the Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding (TUGB) framework. TUGB integrates generative sequence modeling with Reinforcement Learning (RL). It employs a two-stage pipeline where a pre-trained Generative Bidding Model is fine-tuned via an ensemble-based Uncertainty-aware Environment Model. This approach quantifies epistemic uncertainty to penalize high-risk trajectories and evolves the policy from RTG-conditioning to direct bidding optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TUGB significantly outperforms SOTA baselines. Notably, full-scale deployment on JD Search Ad achieved a 2.32\% increase in cost and 3.57\% in target cost, validating its industrial efficacy, while its successful adaptation to subsequent mechanism upgrades and JD Food Delivery Ad further validates TUGB's superior generalization capability.

title: AdaAlloc: Adaptive Visual Token Allocation for Long-Video Question Answering
text: Title: AdaAlloc: Adaptive Visual Token Allocation for Long-Video Question Answering Joungbin An , Kristen Grauman Comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Project page: this https URL Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) Long-video question answering forces multimodal large language models to reason under strict visual-token budgets, creating a tradeoff between broad temporal coverage and fine-grained spatial detail. Uniform sampling preserves coverage but often obscures decisive local cues, while caption-based or frame-similarity retrieval operates over lossy proxies that can miss motion, state changes, and before-after relations. We recast long-video reasoning as a visual-token allocation problem: given a fixed budget, decide how much to spend on global context versus high-resolution local evidence, and where in the video to draw that local evidence from. We introduce AdaAlloc, a training-free inference framework that adaptively allocates visual tokens between a global video overview and localized visual detail. AdaAlloc first plans a global/local allocation policy, then uses temporal grounding to locate candidate evidence segments and refines them into a compact temporal memory. The selected policy controls both frame sampling density and resolution, combining sparse, lower-resolution global frames with denser, higher-resolution local frames drawn from the refined memory. The final answerer reasons over the allocated global context and refined local evidence. Across LVBench, MLVU, VideoMME, and LongVideoBench, AdaAlloc improves over budget-matched uniform sampling by up to 10.5 percentage points and outperforms the compared frame-selection and agentic methods on their reported benchmarks.

title: Two-Layer Evolutionary Scheduling for Machine Learning Jobs in Multi-Cluster Environments
text: Title: Two-Layer Evolutionary Scheduling for Machine Learning Jobs in Multi-Cluster Environments Jingyuan Xu , Changwu Huang , Lemeng Pan , Ke Tang , Xin Yao Subjects: Neural and Evolutionary Computing (cs.NE) ; Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing (cs.DC) The rapid growth of large-scale machine learning (ML) workloads has led to unprecedented demands on GPU cluster scheduling systems. However, existing heuristic schedulers struggle to handle the complexity and dynamics of multi-cluster GPU environments, often leading to load imbalance, long queuing delays, and poor alignment to business objectives. This paper formulates the ML scheduling problem in multi-cluster GPU environments as online multi-objective optimization that minimizes the average and maximum weighted queuing times while maximizing GPU time utilization. To solve this optimization problem, we propose EVO-GP, a two-layer evolutionary online scheduling method that decouples global job-to-cluster allocation from intra-cluster GPU resource allocation. At the job-to-cluster allocation layer, an evolutionary algorithm assigns arriving jobs to feasible clusters to promote load balance across clusters. At the resource allocation layer, a priority function automatically learned offline via genetic programming is used to rank jobs and guide GPU allocation within each cluster. Extensive experiments on both real-world data and simulated workloads demonstrate that the proposed EVO-GP method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining superior adaptability and scalability.

title: AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs
text: Title: AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs Jonas Oppenlaender , Johanna M. Silvennoinen Comments: 21 pages, 2 figures, 13 tables Subjects: Computation and Language (cs.CL) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for creative tasks such as writing, design, and idea generation. For these uses, it matters whether a model's ideas depart from familiar examples or stay close to them. Novelty is one standard measure of creativity, and current creativity evaluations ask human experts or LLM judges to rate how novel an output is. However, these ratings have no fixed reference for what counts as novel (or, in other terms, departure from the familiar). Measuring this departure requires a task with known familiar defaults. The structured imagination task from cognitive psychology is such a task. In this creativity test, people imagine a creature from another planet. The departure from features of Earth animals, such as bilateral symmetry and legs as mode of locomotion, is used as measure of creativity. We introduce AlienBench, a benchmark that adapts the structured imagination task to language models. Models describe alien creatures, and a panel of three LLM judges extracts ten biological features from the description and labels them as either Earth-typical or a departure. The sum of feature departures is the score of a description, from 0 to 10. Each model describes alien creatures under six prompt conditions that vary the framing of the task and the planetary environment. Each model generates 30 descriptions per condition (180 in total), and its overall score is the mean across these descriptions. We evaluate 10 language models, from frontier to open-weight models. Overall scores range from 3.28 (GPT-6 Luna) to 6.55 (Ministral 3 14B). Interestingly, open-weight models score higher than proprietary models in this task (5.40 vs. 4.58). Under the baseline prompt, the models depart from Earth defaults more often on average than 100 human participants on every feature. We release all prompts, generations, judge outputs, and scores.

title: Trajectory Forcing: Exploiting Diffusion Trajectories for Autoregressive Long Video Generation
text: Title: Trajectory Forcing: Exploiting Diffusion Trajectories for Autoregressive Long Video Generation Bohan Wang , Shuo Chen , Yunzhi Li , Zhaozheng Chen , Junzhe Zhang , Hanwang Zhang Comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Autoregressive (AR) modeling is arguably the only way to extend a fixed-length video diffusion model to longer or even streaming videos. However, existing AR diffusion methods use only the previously predicted chunk as context for the next, discarding the intermediate predictions that constitute the chunk's generation history. In contrast, conventional AR models such as LLMs condition on the entire history of preceding tokens. To this end, we propose Trajectory Forcing (TraF), an AR diffusion method that exploits the denoising trajectories of previous video chunks as context. TraF operates under two training regimes: (1) with ground-truth videos, where pseudo-trajectories are constructed from Gaussian interpolations and re-predicted by the model, and (2) with a teacher model, where real trajectories are obtained from the student's own denoising rollout. The first regime naturally provides a strong initialization for the second. On the 5-second VBench benchmark, TraF achieves a Total score of 85.15, outperforming Self Forcing (+0.84) and Causal Forcing (+1.11), with Quality and Semantic improving simultaneously. On 30-second generation---6$\times$ the training horizon---TraF achieves the highest overall quality among all compared methods.

title: BayesCrop: Real-Time Probabilistic Multi-Crop Video Reframing
text: Title: BayesCrop: Real-Time Probabilistic Multi-Crop Video Reframing Cheng-Han Lee , Rajesh Sureddi , Neil Birkbeck , Yilin Wang , Balu Adsumilli , Alan Bovik Comments: This paper is accepted by WACV 2027. We plan to publicly release the source code at this https URL Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Automatic video reframing is increasingly important for adapting landscape content to heterogeneous display formats. Existing methods typically predict a single deterministic crop, despite the subjective nature of reframing and the presence of multiple plausible regions of interest. We present \textbf{BayesCrop}, a real-time probabilistic framework for multi-crop video reframing. BayesCrop represents crop preferences using a two-component spatially isotropic Gaussian mixture over crop position and scale. Each component defines a representative reframing mode together with its local uncertainty, enabling both dual-view prediction and sampling of additional plausible crop candidates. For efficient video processing, we introduce an anchor-and-propagate strategy that performs neural prediction only on sparse anchor frames and propagates crop trajectories using motion vectors available from the compressed video bitstream. The resulting trajectories can be combined into a single output using a lightweight periodic view-switching strategy. Experiments on LIVE-YT-MC, LIVE-YT-VC++, and a multi-target long-video benchmark demonstrate competitive single-output localization, high multi-crop reference coverage, diverse yet coherent crop hypotheses, and stable perceptual quality. BayesCrop achieves real-time throughput of 112 FPS at the default operating point, while sampling from the learned distributions further improves reference coverage beyond the two representative crop means.

title: COMBIO: Automated Discovery of a Compact Composite Biomarker from Routine Laboratory Panels
text: Title: COMBIO: Automated Discovery of a Compact Composite Biomarker from Routine Laboratory Panels Tomer D. Meirman , Lior S. Rokach , Bracha Shapira , Seffi Cohen , Noa Dagan Comments: 27 pages including supplementary material; 4 figures Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) Machine-learning models based on routine laboratory panels can predict outcomes but can be difficult to interpret and operationalize. We present COMBIO, an automated pipeline that distils such a model into a compact closed-form biomarker. The composite is a product of laboratory measurements raised to integer powers from minus two to two. The sign of each exponent indicates whether higher values of the corresponding measurement increase or decrease the composite. Shapley additive explanation values from the gradient-boosted reference model rank five candidate measurements and guide eligible exponent signs. An exhaustive search over small integer exponents selects the formula on an inner validation set, before evaluation on the reserved test set. We evaluated COMBIO across six tasks: three National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey outcomes, liver-disease classification in the Indian Liver Patient Dataset, and Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV in-hospital mortality and sepsis case-finding, with external evaluation in the eICU Collaborative Research Database for the two hospital tasks. Across the six test sets, COMBIO's area under the receiver operating characteristic curve differed by at most 0.03 from logistic regression using the five candidate laboratory measurements. The hospital mortality composite had an area under the curve of 0.698 in the external database. A version restricted to widely available measurements in the source hospital database achieved an area under the curve of 0.786 in a cohort covering 92% of admissions. The multiplicative representation provides compactness rather than additional accuracy, and local validation and recalibration are required before clinical use.

title: PhoPunct: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Transformer Architectures for Vietnamese Punctuation Restoration
text: Title: PhoPunct: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Transformer Architectures for Vietnamese Punctuation Restoration Khoa D. Nguyen , Thai Bao Huynh , Binh T. Nguyen Comments: Accepted at PACLIC 40 (2026) Subjects: Computation and Language (cs.CL) Vietnamese punctuation restoration is often evaluated on relatively small benchmarks, limiting conclusions about how architectural choices scale with data volume. We present a controlled benchmark on News and Novels corpora containing 22.1 million labeled tokens (19.9M News and 2.2M Novels). We evaluate 17 architectures formed from four pretrained Transformer backbones and optional bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and conditional random field (CRF) layers, together with a PhoBERT-large-Bi-LSTM-CRF model, PhoPunct. Every model is trained for eight epochs with the same learning rate and without architecture-specific tuning. Under this fixed budget, adding Bi-LSTM and CRF layers does not reliably improve macro F1: in seven of eight matched domain-backbone comparisons, a plain Transformer classifier matches or outperforms its Bi-LSTM-CRF counterpart. PhoPunct obtains the best News result (61.35), whereas XLM-R with a CRF obtains the best Novels result (50.18), exceeding PhoPunct (48.97). These results show that the value of recurrent and structured-prediction heads depends on their optimization regime and motivate explicit separation between architectural improvements and improvements due to architecture-specific tuning. Our source code is available at: this https URL

title: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation
text: Title: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation Weikang Wang , Haiyang Liu , Xin Zhou , Jun Liu , Weifeng Zhang Comments: Accepted at SIGMOD 2027 Subjects: Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing (cs.DC) The context lengths of large language models (LLMs) are rapidly increasing in real-world applications such as agentic systems and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). To accelerate LLM inference in these scenarios, reusing position-independent key-value (KV) caches across requests has emerged as a promising approach. This technique typically relies on recomputing a selected subset of tokens to restore cross-chunk interactions. However, existing solutions suffer from critical limitations in both algorithmic efficiency and system deployment. Algorithmically, they overlook the distribution of KV cache deviations, leading to either high token-selection overhead or degraded generation quality. At the system level, the reliance on custom LLM execution flows for recomputation complicates deployment and prevents seamless integration with highly optimized inference engines. In this paper, we propose DARIC (\textbf{D}istribution-\textbf{A}ware \textbf{R}ecomputation for \textbf{I}ndependent KV \textbf{C}ache Reuse), a novel KV cache reuse method based on system-algorithm co-design. At its core, DARIC introduces a distribution-aware token selection strategy that adaptively schedules token recomputation based on empirical KV deviation patterns, striking an optimal balance between generation quality and computational efficiency. Moreover, DARIC is built on a lightweight system architecture that enables independent KV cache generation and recomputation with minimal integration overhead, fully preserving existing system-level optimizations of standard inference engines. Comprehensive experiments across various datasets and LLMs demonstrate that DARIC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 1.1$\times$--4.5$\times$ speedup in time-to-first-token (TTFT) with negligible loss in generation quality. Code is available at this https URL .

title: Safe Circumnavigation on Heterogeneous Orbits: A Range-Only HOCBF-QP Framework for Nonholonomic Multi-Agent Systems
text: Title: Safe Circumnavigation on Heterogeneous Orbits: A Range-Only HOCBF-QP Framework for Nonholonomic Multi-Agent Systems Shubham Singh , Anand Singh , Anjali Tiwari , Lara Briñón-Arranz , Katsuki Fujisawa Subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) ; Systems and Control (eess.SY) Circumnavigating a stationary target with a team of robots requires each robot to hold its own standoff distance, to stay evenly spaced from its neighbours, and to avoid collisions with the target and with each other at every instant. The task becomes arduous when the robots are assigned different orbital radii, as their sensors or roles may demand. This paper presents a safety-critical control framework for this problem. Each robot commands both its acceleration and its turn-rate, measures only its distance to the target, and exchanges information only with its two ring neighbours. The design has three features. First, a structural property of the model lets one control law serve every robot regardless of its assigned radius. Second, the acceleration drives each radius exactly to its target, while the turn-rate balances the formation with the neighbours. Third, a higher-order control-barrier-function quadratic program enforces target, geofence, and inter-robot safety on both inputs at once; it leaves the nominal controller untouched away from the constraints and stays valid while the unmeasured range rate is still being estimated. Simulations confirm these guarantees. In a comparison, the closest existing multi-orbit design, even with full state information, violates both the target standoff and the inter-robot margin, whereas the proposed controller does not.

title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use
text: Title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use Chuxue Cao , Jingru Zeng , Boqin Yin , Yujin Zhou , Yidan Huang , Sujin Chen , Jinluan Yang , Haoran Li , Yike Guo , Sirui Han Subjects: Cryptography and Security (cs.CR) ; Machine Learning (cs.LG) LLM agents can exceed their authorization boundaries while pursuing user goals without an adversary. We formalize this phenomenon as authorization drift across data, tool, scope, and time, and introduce the Authorization Drift Benchmark (ADB): 648 samples across seven domains, each pairing a sufficient compliant path with an attractive unauthorized shortcut. To ensure executable tasks, tempting shortcuts, and feasible compliant paths, Staged Execution-Reflective Synthesis (SERS) grounds benchmark validation in real agent rollouts rather than LLM self-critique. Across 13 LLMs and three frameworks (25,207 trajectories), greater capability accompanies greater drift, with frontier-capable models exhibiting drift rates of 0.43 to 0.61. Yet 86.18% of tasks admit an observed clean-success trajectory, showing that drift is avoidable. Drift is persistent and dominated by early data over-collection; apparent improvements under agentic scaffolds coincide with collapsing clean-completion performance. To understand potential harms to individuals and society, we map drift points to legal provisions across four jurisdictions, connecting overreach to privacy and information-security concerns. Data minimisation is the most frequently implicated provision, and 93.5% of legally grounded drifting runs map to multiple jurisdictions, making the potential consequences of authorization drift more interpretable.

title: PathXAI: Evidence-guided structured pathology reporting by transferable tissue segmentation
text: Title: PathXAI: Evidence-guided structured pathology reporting by transferable tissue segmentation Zhaorui Tan , Jun Aun Tan , Weixiang Zhong , Xiaoxi Wang , Tan Pan , Xingdong Xue , Li Liu , Jing Zhang , Jing Zhang , Weimiao Yu Comments: More experimental results will be added in the future version Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) ; Computation and Language (cs.CL) Pathology reporting requires translating tissue observations across regions and slides into specific diagnoses and supporting morphological descriptions. However, the use of explicit tissue-composition measurements to guide H&E-based report generation remains underexplored. Thus, we developed PathXAI, which combines segmentation-derived tissue information with H&E images and optional domain knowledge to guide diagnostic reasoning, targeted reinspection and structured report writing. Its segmentation component exceeded baselines in mean Dice on internal and external tests. In automated report evaluation on 1,200 public and 151 private cases, PathXAI achieved higher agreement with reference diagnoses and documented morphology than the H&E-based comparators. On the public evaluation cohort, PathXAI-Report exceeded Qwen + H&E in cancer family match rate by 4.4 percentage points and in finding F1 by 5.7 percentage points. PathXAI generates evidence-linked reports with a self-hosted pretrained vision-language model, without updating its weights.

title: Finite-sample Calibration Guarantees for Binary Segmentation
text: Title: Finite-sample Calibration Guarantees for Binary Segmentation Bruno Viti , Martin Holler Comments: Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research 10/2026 Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) ; Machine Learning (cs.LG) Machine learning based segmentation models are frequently miscalibrated, producing for each pixel a label prediction whose associated confidence does not accurately reflect the true underlying probability. This limitation is particularly critical in high-stakes applications such as medical image segmentation. Although several calibration methods have been proposed, only a small subset of them provides theoretical guarantees on the calibration error, i.e., they do not typically ensure that, with high probability, the model exhibits a low calibration error. In this work, we develop a post-hoc calibration method for which formal calibration guarantees can be established. To achieve this, we derive from standard concentration inequalities an improved theoretical bound that explicitly accounts for the spatial dependence inherent in binary segmentation outputs. We empirically demonstrate that the proposed calibrator satisfies the derived guarantee and outperforms existing post-hoc calibration approaches.

title: CoMET: Tracking the Shared Pose Error of Roadside Messages for Asynchronous Vehicle-Infrastructure Cooperative 3D Detection
text: Title: CoMET: Tracking the Shared Pose Error of Roadside Messages for Asynchronous Vehicle-Infrastructure Cooperative 3D Detection Shuwei Sun , Jian Huang , Hui Cao Comments: 25 pages, 4 figures. Code and experimental results archived at this https URL Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) A roadside sensor can detect vehicles hidden from the ego vehicle, but a pose error shifts every detection in the same message. We study asynchronous vehicle-infrastructure cooperative 3D detection on V2X-Seq using only information available at decision time, without ground truth, future frames, or per-pair calibration offsets at inference. Objects seen by both sensors reveal the shared translation, but even at zero added delay, 38% of validation messages have no matched pair. We propose CoMET (Common-Mode Error Tracking), which estimates this translation over time. At each message arrival, CoMET matches vehicle and roadside detections, estimates the offset from mutually nearest pairs, and updates a Kalman filter for that sender. When no pair matches, the filter carries its estimate forward. The correction applies to all roadside boxes, including those unseen by the ego vehicle. The estimator has no learned parameters; a separate frozen head ranks the merged detections. Across four delays from 0 to 400 ms on 21 validation sequences, CoMET averages 66.63 bird's-eye-view AP at IoU 0.7, compared with 63.18 for the same late fusion using uncorrected online poses and 62.96 for the best intermediate-fusion baseline. Across five detectors from three architectures, CoMET gains 2.2 to 3.5 AP points over online poses and 0.3 to 0.6 over estimating the offset from the current message alone. We find that the benchmark uses a zero offset as a placeholder in 28% of validation messages and that its offset search reaches the boundary in 45% of the rest. These offsets affect the labels for objects seen only from the roadside. Under two alternative label references, CoMET improves on uncorrected online poses in every evaluated population. Retraining intermediate fusion with CoMET poses and corrected labels improves detection on all three architectures tested, with statistically significant gains on two.

title: Improving Large Audio-Language Model Embedding Baselines for Instruction-Aware Speech Retrieval
text: Title: Improving Large Audio-Language Model Embedding Baselines for Instruction-Aware Speech Retrieval Chen-An Li , Cheng-Han Chiang , Hung-yi Lee Comments: Code and artifacts will be uploaded to this https URL Subjects: Sound (cs.SD) Speech retrieval finds relevant spoken documents given a spoken query. The spoken query alone may not reveal the retrieval goal, such as finding an answer or matching speaker identity. Instruction-aware speech retrieval expresses this goal through a natural-language text instruction. Large audio-language models (LALMs) effectively process speech and text, and our analysis shows that different retrieval requirements favor hidden states from different audio-encoder layers.
