We introduce IRIS-Embed, which adapts LALMs into embedding models through contrastive training and instruction-aware audio layer weighting. We construct about 900K training samples from real data and synthetic data, with instructions expressing requirements for one or more speech attributes. On INSPIRE, an instruction-aware speech retrieval benchmark, IRIS-Embed consistently outperforms the corresponding LALM baselines. The best model achieves 62.92% macro-average Recall@50, surpassing the strongest baseline at 45.15%. Controlled comparisons demonstrate instruction awareness and the benefits of audio layer weighting. On MAEB, a massive audio embedding benchmark, macro-average gains of 9.4-19.8 points over the corresponding baselines show generalization beyond speech retrieval.

title: Look Closer, Align Better: Explicit Visual Attributes for Robust EEG-to-Image Decoding
text: Title: Look Closer, Align Better: Explicit Visual Attributes for Robust EEG-to-Image Decoding Ke Xiao , Banghua Yang , Wenbin Guo , Fenqi Rong Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) EEG-to-image retrieval commonly aligns neural responses with representations from pretrained vision encoders. However, these representations may underrepresent fine-grained visual details needed to distinguish semantically similar images. To address this limitation, we first investigate the EEG decodability and complementary predictive value of explicit visual attributes, identifying visual cues that capture EEG-relevant information beyond pretrained representations. Building on these findings, we propose AttrEcho, a framework that enriches pretrained visual representations with complementary, spatially aligned visual attributes. Specifically, Region-Aligned Visual Attribute Fusion (RAVF) integrates EEG-relevant local visual attributes with spatially corresponding pretrained features through a learnable signed residual gate. We further employ Feature Token Aggregation (FTA), which learns dimension-specific weights across regions to aggregate refined visual features for contrastive alignment with EEG representations. Experiments on THINGS-EEG demonstrate that AttrEcho achieves 94.8% Top-1 and 99.7% Top-5 accuracy in intra-subject 200-way retrieval, while maintaining 82.1% Top-1 accuracy as the gallery expands to 1,600 images with same-concept distractors. AttrEcho also achieves 25.3% Top-1 and 53.0% Top-5 accuracy in inter-subject retrieval. These results highlight the importance of EEG-relevant visual attributes and spatially aligned fusion for fine-grained EEG-to-image retrieval.

title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
text: Title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence Chao Liang , Ke Chen , Fengxiaoxiao Li , Shibo Huang , Yufeng Sun , Zhaokai Yin , Jianhuan Lai , Haozhe Feng , Chenghuan Jia , Zhipeng Zhang Subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success. On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system. Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5. In long-horizon pour-over coffee preparation, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion at two filter-handling steps from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%, compared with A2-WLA retries. Our training infrastructure delivers 427.1 samples per second, 4.03x the throughput of a pi0.5 reference implementation on matched hardware. We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning.

title: PAGSL: Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning for explainable scholar recommendation
text: Title: PAGSL: Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning for explainable scholar recommendation Jiale Xu , Mingshu Ai , Junjie Huang , Tao Jia Comments: 24pages, 12 figures Journal-ref: Information Processing and Management, 63, 104826, 2026 Subjects: Information Retrieval (cs.IR) ; Social and Information Networks (cs.SI) Explainable scholar recommendation aims to identify potential scholars of interest and provide reasonable explanations for the recommendations. However, existing frameworks struggle with optimization-induced noise and "hub node bias", yielding trivial explanations that lack hierarchical depth and personalization. To this end, we propose a novel explainable scholar recommendation model, Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning (named PAGSL). PAGSL combines representation learning and semantic path knowledge to ensure recommendation performance while providing interpretable results from two perspectives. Specifically, it activates latent academic paths among entities through graph augmentation and employs a path-based neural network to encode these paths for recommendation. A masking mechanism with path score optimization is designed to generate concise and informative explanations. We evaluate PAGSL on three academic datasets (Scholat, AMiner, and ResearchGate), comprising approximately 49,000 authors and over 330,000 interaction records. Experimental evaluations validate that PAGSL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant improvements of 6.31\% in F1-score, 6.29\% in Accuracy and 5.95\% in AUC for recommendation. Crucially, in terms of explainability, we provide quantitative results and visualization effects. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our heterogeneous convolution and path representation learning. PAGSL achieves strong performance in both recommendation accuracy and explainability.

title: TouchAnnotator: Multi-Source Tactile Supervision with Privileged-View Distillation
text: Title: TouchAnnotator: Multi-Source Tactile Supervision with Privileged-View Distillation Ao Li , Zhihao Yuan , Chubin Zhang , Kunrui Huang , Sheng Xu , Zengjue Chen , Junjie Wang , Jiawei Li , Yansong Tang Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Egocentric video captures human-object interaction at scale but rarely includes tactile labels for hidden contact and pressure. We introduce TouchAnnotator, an ego-only bimanual tactile annotator trained with multi-source tactile supervision and privileged-view distillation. A canonical hand field unifies glove pressure, geometry-derived human contact, and robot fingertip deformation from six datasets and three embodiments, while source-aware masks preserve valid targets. During training, an EMA teacher observes synchronized ego and wrist views and distills hand-local representations and tactile predictions into a student that uses only ego video and estimated pose at inference. Compact past-clip memory supplies temporal context. We evaluate on EgoTouch, zero-shot FPHA transfer, and 860 synchronized glove recordings. The model transfers to bare-hand contact and produces qualitatively coherent tactile responses across bare-hand, gloved-hand, and robot embodiments. On measured recordings, it improves temporal accuracy by 5.38 points and Volumetric IoU by 5.02 points under a shared protocol. These results show that heterogeneous human--robot supervision and privileged training views can turn egocentric video into dense tactile annotations.

title: Auditing Grasp Feasibility Predictors with Planner-Verified Counterfactuals
text: Title: Auditing Grasp Feasibility Predictors with Planner-Verified Counterfactuals Sajid Ansari , Antony Thomas , Girish Varma Comments: Accepted to WACV 2027. 10 pages main paper + 8 pages supplementary Subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) Grasp-feasibility predictors report near-perfect accuracy on Task and Motion Planning benchmarks, but high accuracy on these benchmarks does not verify that a predictor uses the collision geometry that the motion planner checks. We propose a planner-verified counterfactual (CF) test: holding the grasp pose fixed, we insert a solid obstacle into the approach corridor, add its points to the model input, and let a planner re-derive the label, which flips from feasible to infeasible. Across eight predictors spanning point clouds, voxels, depth, and object tokens, CF-pair AUROC falls from high natural AUROC (0.920-0.996) to chance (0.470-0.504), and the flip holds across four planners, two arms, and a real-object obstacle. Predictors fail at different resolutions, from a bounding box to a 12.5 cm voxel. In the point-cloud models we dissect, the obstacle either moves the representation in a direction unrelated to whether it blocks the grasp or is not registered at all. A clearance-aware read of the corridor points, trained on the unmodified benchmark with no counterfactual scenes, reaches 0.983 CF-pair AUROC, but it remains bound to its trained obstacle placements; a placement-invariant clearance representation is still open. We release the counterfactual labels, metrics, datasheet, and relabeling pipeline at this https URL .

title: DINO-Nucleus: Multi-Level Self-Supervised Features for Nucleus Instance Segmentation
text: Title: DINO-Nucleus: Multi-Level Self-Supervised Features for Nucleus Instance Segmentation Mohammad Sarhangzadeh , Elyar Esmaeilzadeh , Doruk Oner Comments: 10 pages, 2 figures Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Nucleus instance segmentation and counting are essential for quantitative microscopy, enabling reliable analysis of cell populations, tissue organization, and disease-related changes. However, accurately separating touching nuclei remains difficult, and many existing approaches rely on complex models or sensitive post-processing procedures. We present DINO-Nucleus, a parameter-efficient framework that leverages multi-level self-supervised DINOv2 representations for nucleus instance segmentation and counting. The model jointly predicts nucleus regions, pixel-wise instance flows, and explicit nucleus centers, while a consistency objective encourages the predicted flows to converge toward their corresponding centers. Multi-level transformer features provide complementary spatial and semantic information, and the pretrained backbone is adapted using lightweight LoRA modules to reduce fine-tuning cost. Experimental results show that DINO-Nucleus achieves strong segmentation and counting performance with parameter-efficient backbone adaptation. These findings demonstrate that parameter-efficient adaptation of multi-level self-supervised features can provide an effective solution for nucleus instance segmentation in microscopy images.

title: Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise
text: Title: Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise Ziyi Lei , Houqi Su Subjects: Numerical Analysis (math.NA) We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete method of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise. Using the Cole-Hopf transformation, the equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a regularized inverse Cole-Hopf transformation. The analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with the positivity and inverse-moment bounds for the transformed solution. For additive space-time white noise, the numerical method achieves mean-square convergence rates arbitrarily close to 1/2 in space and 1/4 in time. The rates are slower when the noises are rougher.

title: Shortest Synchronizing Words on Product Automata
text: Title: Shortest Synchronizing Words on Product Automata Henning Fernau , Igor Rystsov Subjects: Formal Languages and Automata Theory (cs.FL) We consider some operations on finite automata graphs, in particular various product, union and merge operations, and investigate how they relate to the parameter~$\mathrm{rt}$, the \emph{length of a shortest synchronizing word}. We derive some lower and upper bounds for the operations that we study. We also examine several classes of automata (for instance, partially ordered, commutative or idempotent automata) that are preserved under these operations and show in which way the parameter $\mathrm{rt}$ behaves in these automata classes. Also, we consider automata classes that can be constructed by combining automata from better known classes; in particular, these new classes of automata will also satisfy the bound of the famous Černý conjecture. This also motivates us to study even more closure properties. In particular, we show that certain automata classes related to synchronization form pseudo-varieties. We also commence a similar study concerning the length of shortest homing sequences of Mealy automata.

title: Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification
text: Title: Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification Zetao Fei , Josselin Garnier Subjects: Numerical Analysis (math.NA) ; Mathematical Physics (math-ph) We consider the inverse problem of determining the location, orientation, shape, and material parameters of a small elastic inclusion embedded in a homogeneous medium from full-aperture measurements of the scattered field. Using a small-volume expansion, we derive explicit leading-order expressions for four Kirchhoff migration imaging functionals, denoted by PP, PS, SP, and SS, corresponding to the four combinations of pressure (P) and shear (S) waves used for receiver- and source-side backpropagation. The resulting point-spread functions quantitatively characterize the resolution of each mode and show that the SS mode achieves the highest spatial resolution. For an elliptic inclusion, we show that the PP mode uniquely determines the elastic moment tensor (EMT) within the leading-order asymptotic model, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the material and geometric parameters of the inclusion. For a general small scatterer, the reconstruction may instead be interpreted as an effective elliptic representation determined by its leading-order EMT. For a disk, the parameter-identification problem is underdetermined; nevertheless, explicit upper and lower bounds on its volume are derived. We further analyze the model error arising from neglected cross-mode contributions when the distance from the center of the measurement configuration is not sufficiently large relative to the elastic wavelengths. Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed imaging and reconstruction methods.

title: Deep Learning Theory through the Lens of Statistical Physics: A Topical Review
text: Title: Deep Learning Theory through the Lens of Statistical Physics: A Topical Review Wei Huang , Youjin Deng Comments: 22 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Topical review published in Front. Phys. 22(1), 011302 (2027); this version contains minor corrections Journal-ref: Front. Phys. 22(1), 011302 (2027) Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Statistical Mechanics (cond-mat.stat-mech) The recent success of foundation models and deep learning has far outpaced our theoretical understanding of how large-scale neural networks learn and generalize. Statistical physics provides a natural language for describing such high-dimensional, nonlinear, and strongly coupled systems, offering concepts such as mean-field theory, phase transitions, energy landscapes, and stochastic dynamics. In this topical review, we adopt a statistical-physics way of thinking -- from concepts including phases and criticality, and free-energy viewpoints, to methods such as kernel and Gaussian-process limits, mean-field and dynamical mean-field theories, random-matrix tools, and Fokker-Planck formalisms, and to a mindset emphasizing universality, scaling, and tractable limits with explicit validity regimes. We survey recent progress on understanding modern deep learning through this lens, including mean-field analyses of wide networks, spectral and geometric perspectives on loss landscapes, stochastic-gradient-based training viewed as a dynamical process, and phase-transition analogies that organize phenomena such as overparameterization, generalization, and representation change. Our goal is to synthesize these threads into a coherent framework that clarifies what each approximation explains, when it is expected to hold, and how apparently competing narratives relate or diverge. Together, these perspectives form a unified physical framework that views representation learning as a collective phenomenon in high-dimensional systems, bridging deterministic and stochastic regimes of gradient-based optimization.

title: CARGO: Causal Attribution and Responsibility-Guided Preventive Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving
text: Title: CARGO: Causal Attribution and Responsibility-Guided Preventive Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving Jingjia Teng , Yang Li , Wenjie Huang Comments: Abridged version containing the main results; the full version is under peer review and will be updated here upon acceptance Subjects: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) This study presents Causal Attribution and Responsibility-Guided Optimization (CARGO), a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for cooperative on-ramp merging in mixed traffic. A shared latent-context posterior and an action-conditioned response model estimate directed behavioral influence, with posterior uncertainty propagated into interaction-edge selection. Complementary attribution mechanisms couple signed influence with marginal team utility for cooperative reward shaping and assign responsibility from positive excess tail risk relative to a safe reference policy. Conditional diffusion generates future responses for action-dependent risk estimation. Responsibility-guided preventive optimization calibrates agent-specific risk-reduction requirements to local capacity within a policy trust region, using reserved safety margins, adaptive requirement scaling, and joint feasibility verification. Theoretical analysis establishes risk monotonicity and sufficient local conditions for non-decreasing environmental return under explicit assumptions. Experiments in highway-env across three traffic densities, together with controlled graph-recovery and attribution studies, support the effectiveness of the framework. Under high-density traffic, CARGO increases the success rate by 66.04\% and reduces the crash rate by 56.23\% relative to the best evaluated baseline for each metric.

title: SPDMX: Large-Scale Open Stem Audio From Symbolic Music
text: Title: SPDMX: Large-Scale Open Stem Audio From Symbolic Music Phillip Long , Eduardo Escoto , Julian McAuley , Zachary Novack Comments: 4 pages, 3 figures, 1 table Subjects: Sound (cs.SD) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Multimedia (cs.MM); Audio and Speech Processing (eess.AS) Large public datasets have driven recent progress in machine learning, from text and vision to speech and general audio. Music remains an outlier, as copyright blocks redistribution of training audio, while many modern tasks need individual stems rather than mixtures. Existing multitrack resources trade off realism, scale, and licensing, while synthetic alternatives rely on proprietary VSTs or naive open rendering that yields weak stems. We introduce SPDMX, a listening-guided rendering of public-domain PDMX scores into an openly-licensed stem corpus with aligned scores and an open render pipeline: $253{,}982$ songs, $490{,}159$ mono stems, and $5{,}469$ song-hours at $44.1$ kHz under CC BY 4.0, with paired MIDI and identifiers linking to PDMX metadata. $88{,}403$ songs ($34.8\%$; $2{,}734$ song-hours) provide multitrack supervision. To our knowledge, this is the largest openly-licensed synthetic multitrack subset by song-hours, enabling source separation, stem-conditioned synthesis, MIDI-to-audio, transcription, and joint symbolic-audio modeling. We release the corpus, metadata, and open pipeline for reuse on other symbolic collections. Demos and experimental notes are on the project page.

title: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics
text: Title: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics Yubo Song , Pascal A. Schirmer , Subham Sahoo Comments: The manuscript has been accepted for publication in the Proceedings of 2026 IEEE Design Methodologies Conference (DMC 2026) Subjects: Emerging Technologies (cs.ET) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Neural and Evolutionary Computing (cs.NE); Systems and Control (eess.SY) Artificial intelligence for power electronics is evolving toward a deeper comprehension of system intrinsic behaviors and dynamics. As a novel integration of neural computation and electric circuits, spike-based neuromorphic computing offers promising potential in high energy efficiency and adaptability for data-driven applications. Building on the latency-coding principles, this article proposes a framework for data-light condition monitoring that relies solely on three-phase AC current measurements. The AC current signals are encoded as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons, which are inherently compatible with spiking neural networks that can effectively facilitate the estimation of device parameters. Case studies are presented to validate the performances, while constraints and further optimizations are also evaluated and discussed, and future extensions of the methodology are provided.

title: Learning Generative Dynamics for 3D Molecule Generation via Sequential Neuro-Symbolic Constraints
text: Title: Learning Generative Dynamics for 3D Molecule Generation via Sequential Neuro-Symbolic Constraints Zhuoran Li , Xu Sun , Chang Wen Chen , Wanyu Lin Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) Diffusion models have recently emerged as a powerful paradigm for generating 3D molecules. Despite showing remarkable promise, they learn atomic distributions implicitly from data, without explicitly encoding physicochemical rules into their generative dynamics. Consequently, generated samples can be statistically plausible yet chemically invalid. To address this problem, we propose Sequential Neuro-Symbolic Constrained Diffusion (SensDiff), a framework that integrates symbolic rules into generative modeling, enabling the model to internalize scientific priors during training. Central to SensDiff is the observation that the diffusion trajectory of 3D molecule generation exhibits a coarse-to-fine evolution: valid molecules arise by first mitigating macroscopic geometric conflicts and then refining structures toward microscopic chemical consistency through iterative denoising. Accordingly, SensDiff mirrors this dynamic by sequentially enforcing constraints with adaptive weighting during training, progressively steering generation toward valid molecular geometries. Moreover, SensDiff translates domain knowledge into interpretable generative controls, grounding opaque neural denoising in scientific principles. Experiments on molecular benchmarks and real-world constrained generation tasks confirm that SensDiff consistently improves chemical validity while adhering to physicochemical rules and user-specified targets. The code is publicly available at this https URL .

title: Augmentron: Scalable Multi-View Visual Augmentation for Robot Learning
text: Title: Augmentron: Scalable Multi-View Visual Augmentation for Robot Learning Tanay Tandon , Aseem Doriwala , Jade Choghari , Catherine Weaver , Pragna Mannam Comments: Accepted to the 8th Robot Learning Workshop (WRL), NeurIPS 2026 Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Robotics (cs.RO) Robot policies trained on visually narrow demonstrations can become sensitive to environmental features that are unrelated to the task. Existing generative augmentation methods can introduce visual diversity, but processing every frame and camera view independently is computationally expensive and may produce inconsistent observations across cameras and timestamps. We introduce Augmentron, a geometry-aware pipeline that generates reusable scene representations and renders them through recorded camera poses. This produces temporally and multi-view consistent environ- ment and workspace variations while preserving the robot, task objects, actions, and annotations. Across three physical manipulation tasks, replacing half of the real world training dataset with Augmentron data improves model success across three tasks for both in out-of-distribution distractor objects, and out-of-distribution workspace variation evaluations. In a separate comparison against alternate augmentation techniques, Augmentron achieves the highest pooled success in all three conditions. The results show that introducing augmented data to a data training recipe can help policies generalize to dynamic real-world settings.

title: BMMS: Policy-Conditioned Measurement of Behavioral Compliance in Language Models
text: Title: BMMS: Policy-Conditioned Measurement of Behavioral Compliance in Language Models Anthony Rhodes , Gadi Singer Comments: 21 pages, 4 figures. NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Trust-AI-Eval (TAE). Artifact: this https URL Subjects: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) ; Computation and Language (cs.CL) Behavioral evaluation of language models fixes its dimensions in advance: hallucination, sycophancy, toxicity, over-refusal. An operator in a regulated industry needs a different question answered: does a system do what a particular rulebook requires? We introduce the Behavioral Misalignment Metric Suite (BMMS), which measures policy-conditioned misalignment by taking a policy corpus as an argument and returning a compliance profile over it, for any published policy and any system that answers in natural language. The Compliance Attainment Score (CAS) measures severity-weighted attainment over the obligations that bind the system, and the Compliance Robustness Margin (CRM) the share of that attainment surviving graded adversarial pressure; Behavioral Invariance (BIV) and the Behavioral Disposition Index (BDI) are specified and released with the suite. Dimensions enter only by passing a published admission test whose binding criterion is attribution: a quantity that moves when the judge changes, holding the target fixed, is measuring the instrument. Applying it excluded one of the quantities the suite itself reported. Across 1,003 obligations from eleven documents in five registers, the admission criterion holds 94.4% precision against blinded human judgment on vendor specifications and 50.0% on analytical guidance, extraction fidelity is 94.6%, and re-scoring under judges from two other providers leaves target ordering invariant while the absolute score of a single target spans up to 0.22. We apply it to the two most detailed published behavioral specifications. Own-specification advantage is not resolved from zero once document difficulty is subtracted, but absolute self-compliance is another matter: GPT-4o fails 70.7% of the hard constraints binding it in the Model Spec published by OpenAI, where the two Claude models fail 0.0% and 9.1% of theirs.

title: Learning When to Think: Dual-Reference Offline Optimization for Adaptive VLM Reasoning
text: Title: Learning When to Think: Dual-Reference Offline Optimization for Adaptive VLM Reasoning Hongbin Lin , Sizhe Zou , Juangui Xu , Xinyue Xu , Zhuoli Ouyang , Stanislav Kolchin , Chengwei Qin , Zhongxiang Dai , Yao Shu Subjects: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) Reasoning traces improve vision-language models on complex multimodal tasks, but forcing every input to follow a long reasoning process leads to overthinking and unnecessary inference cost. We study adaptive fast/slow thinking for VLMs, where one model answers directly for simple inputs and reasons step by step when needed. Fast answers and slow traces often come from distinct behavior policies, making a single-reference offline objective misweight one mode. We propose DUAL-REFERENCE BOLT (DR-BOLT), which distinguishes the desired fast/slow mixture reference from the sampling distribution and corrects their mismatch in reward-weighted training. Fast/slow partition competition explains routing in the optimal target; an efficient source-wise correction approximates the exact objective when response formats are well separated. Matched Qwen3-VL comparisons use identical candidate banks to isolate the objective from slow-teacher quality. DR-BOLT improves score-length trade-offs over the evaluated offline and online baselines on ScienceQA and three held-out transfer benchmarks, with a 24.1% cross-benchmark slow ratio and a 2.90-fold end-to-end training speedup over reproduced GRPO. These results support adaptive reasoning in the studied two-reference setting, while broader robustness remains open. Our code is available at this https URL .

title: Evaluation of a Multi-Link Machine Learning Approach for Rainfall Detection Using Satellite Microwave Links
text: Title: Evaluation of a Multi-Link Machine Learning Approach for Rainfall Detection Using Satellite Microwave Links Mostafa Ftouni , Margherita Spalla , Matteo Colli , Andrea Randazzo , Christian Gianoglio Journal-ref: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters, Volume: 23, article number: 1001305, date of publication: 21 May 2026 Subjects: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) ; Machine Learning (cs.LG); Signal Processing (eess.SP) The impacts of climate change have increased the need for reliable real-time rainfall monitoring systems. This study investigates rainfall detection using a network of opportunistic sensors based on satellite microwave links (SMLs) combined with machine learning (ML) classifiers. Two models, a random forest (RF) and a convolutional neural network (CNN), were trained on aggregated SML data, including information from neighboring links. The results demonstrate that leveraging information from multiple links substantially enhances the detection of both wet and dry periods compared to single-link approaches. Moreover, the RF model consistently provides a more stable and reliable trade-off than CNN, improving rainfall detection and reducing misclassifications overall, with particularly strong performance during harsh weather conditions. The study spanned up to 32 rainy days between 2021 and 2024.

title: Word Subtraction Games
text: Title: Word Subtraction Games Yusuke Inoue , Hiroki Inazu Subjects: Formal Languages and Automata Theory (cs.FL) This note is a self-contained text on word subtraction games, combinatorial games in which players alternately remove a nonempty suffix belonging to a prescribed subtraction set from the current word. It collects and develops basic results on these games from the viewpoints of combinatorial game theory and formal language theory. We focus on the relationship between subtraction sets and the resulting languages of winning and losing positions. The topics include finite, regular, and context-free subtraction sets, as well as several variants and further developments.

title: A Structured-Surrogate Double-Model Approach to Regularization Parameter Selection
text: Title: A Structured-Surrogate Double-Model Approach to Regularization Parameter Selection Malena Español , Markus Juvonen , Samuli Siltanen , Ilaria Trombini , Chuyang Wu Subjects: Numerical Analysis (math.NA) Double-model methods select a regularization parameter by matching the discrepancy between two reconstructions of the same data to a prescribed target. The Structured-Surrogate Double-Model (SSDM) framework is developed around a computationally inexpensive structured surrogate of the forward operator and a spectrally explicit perturbation, with the selected parameter subsequently applied to the original inverse problem. Given a prescribed target, parameter selection requires neither prior knowledge of the noise level nor training data. For a class of Tikhonov regularization problems, the squared discrepancy is shown to attain a strict maximum at zero regularization, decay as $\lambda^{-2}$, and decrease strictly beyond an explicit phase-aware threshold. A complementary, data-dependent certificate is established to guarantee strict monotonicity on finite intervals, enabling unique and reliable target matching even when the global threshold is overly conservative. The discrepancy is further connected to directional roughness in image deblurring, providing a geometric interpretation of the selection principle. Experiments on synthetic images and on synthetically blurred natural photographs illustrate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical applicability of certified parameter selection.

title: UniExit: A Unified Latency-Aware Early-Exit Runtime for Heterogeneous Edge AI
text: Title: UniExit: A Unified Latency-Aware Early-Exit Runtime for Heterogeneous Edge AI Yuhang Guan , Huanle Zhang , Xiaomin Ouyang , Zhidan Liu Comments: 15 pages, 20 figures. Accepted to ACM SenSys 2027 (The International Conference on Embedded Artificial Intelligence and Sensing Systems) Subjects: Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing (cs.DC) Edge applications increasingly combine CNN-based perception with edge-deployable Transformer-based language models, but deploying such heterogeneous workloads on resource-constrained devices is challenging because inference latency varies with both input difficulty and runtime hardware state. Early-exit inference reduces computation by terminating at intermediate stages, yet existing methods are often model-specific and rely on static latency profiles that become stale under dynamic edge conditions. This paper presents UniExit, a unified latency-aware early-exit runtime for heterogeneous edge AI. UniExit abstracts CNN blocks and Transformer layers as ordered stages and applies a common latency-aware routing policy while retaining model-specific quality mechanisms. It predicts the cost of reaching the next exit from runtime state and inference progress to make budget-aware continue-or-exit decisions. UniExit combines runtime-state-aware latency prediction, cache-based prediction reuse, trend-aware fallback, and CNN-specific exit stabilization to provide low-overhead and robust online control. We implement UniExit on multiple edge and edge-cloud platforms and evaluate it with representative CNN and Transformer-based language-model workloads. Across single-workload, concurrent heterogeneous, and edge-cloud settings, UniExit consistently improves deadline satisfaction and latency-accuracy trade-offs over existing progressive inference baselines, while reducing redundant exit-module computation and task-level energy consumption.

title: GreyZone: Production-quality Agentic Application Threats
text: Title: GreyZone: Production-quality Agentic Application Threats Ruoyu Zhou , Shuyao Jiang , Haifeng Ruan , Abhik Roychoudhury Subjects: Software Engineering (cs.SE) Agents are increasingly deployed across domains such as coding, banking, and commerce. Their ability to invoke tools and change application state makes security testing important for reliable deployment. Although agent security has been studied through various adversarial testing approaches, benchmarks grounded in production agent environments remain limited. We introduce GreyZone, a benchmark for evaluating automated red-teaming services against real-world agent applications. Unlike benchmarks such as AgentDojo, which primarily evaluate subject agents under attack, GreyZone evaluates services' ability to generate and deliver attacks that cause verified security-policy violations. We select independently developed, open-source agent applications with security boundaries concerning access permissions, confidentiality, and action authorization. These applications expose diverse attack surfaces, including those arising from multi-agent interactions and multimodal inputs. By grounding evaluation in application environments that preserve production-relevant workflows and independently verifying outcomes, GreyZone supports research on automated agent security testing. Specifically, we present two preliminary case studies using Promptfoo on Letta Code and Clawith to examine attack delivery, agent behavior, and verified outcomes. We release the benchmark, including subject agents and attack surfaces for each application, to support further research on agent testing methods.

title: Rethinking Requirement-to-Code Traceability Through Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Approaches
text: Title: Rethinking Requirement-to-Code Traceability Through Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Approaches Sarthak Banerjee , Sallam Abualhaija , Domenico Bianculli , Lionel Briand Subjects: Computational Engineering, Finance, and Science (cs.CE) Requirements-to-code traceability supports essential software engineering activities, including change impact analysis, maintenance, and regulatory compliance. Existing approaches typically rely on a retrieval-and-classification pipeline, which suffers from an inherent retrieval bottleneck: relevant source files that are not retrieved cannot be recovered during subsequent analysis. In this paper, we revisit requirements-to-code traceability in light of the substantially larger context windows offered by modern large language models, which make repository-scale analysis feasible without a separate retrieval step. We propose three approaches: a single-agent approach that analyzes the entire code repository in one pass, and two multi-agent approaches based on self-verification and multi-agent debate. Our evaluation shows that the single-agent approach substantially improves recall, achieving 80.9%, a gain of 38.6 percentage points (pp) over the state-of-the-art retrieval-based baseline, albeit with a 25.8 pp reduction in precision. By leveraging collaborative reasoning, the multi-agent debate-based approach achieves the best overall precision-recall balance, with 24.5% precision and 71.0% recall, yielding an F2 score of 49.5%. This represents an improvement of 7.5 pp over the state of the art and 2.7 pp over the single-agent approach. While the quantitative evaluation establishes the overall effectiveness of the approaches, the aggregate metrics alone explain little due to the considerable variability across results. Importantly, qualitative analysis provides key insights into highly variable quantitative results: the retrieval approach suits requirements that echo the code's vocabulary; single-agent, full-context reasoning suits well-documented, consistently named code; and multi-agent debate suits indirect, conflicting, or distributed evidence.

title: Beyond the Grid: Continuous Dictionary Pursuit for Interpretable Signal Decomposition
text: Title: Beyond the Grid: Continuous Dictionary Pursuit for Interpretable Signal Decomposition Nick Janssen , Melanie Schaller , Bodo Rosenhahn Comments: 10 pages main paper, 3 pages references, 22 pages appendix, to be published in NeurIPS 2026 Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) Deep learning models achieve high accuracy in signal processing but remain difficult to interpret. Classical matching pursuit and sparse coding offer better transparency but suffer from spectral leakage and grid mismatch when signal frequencies do not align with discrete dictionary atoms. We introduce Continuous Dictionary Pursuit (CDP), a framework for interpretable signal decomposition that learns the parameters of closed-form functions directly from data. CDP optimizes over a continuous manifold of differentiable atoms and, unlike prior continuous pursuit methods that operate on a single analytic family, searches a heterogeneous library spanning periodic, trend, transient, and discontinuous structures. The algorithm employs a greedy iterative strategy using data-driven priors and gradient-based optimization to isolate individual signal components, with discontinuous waveforms made differentiable through spectral sharpness annealing. To ensure a sparse atom set for reconstruction, the framework utilizes a stopping criterion based on a predefined atom budget and residual error convergence. Evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets show that CDP removes the grid discretization error for atom families contained in its library, recovers generative parameters to within $1\%$ on stationary synthetic signals expressible in that library, and achieves the best sparsity-accuracy trade-off among classical, continuous-pursuit, and neural baselines in the sparse regime. Beyond decomposition, we demonstrate that the extracted atoms can serve as structured curriculum targets for training sequence models, improving forecasting accuracy over standard end-to-end training on most evaluated datasets. The method offers a glass-box alternative for signal decomposition by providing high reconstruction fidelity alongside direct physical interpretability.

title: Separating Measures by Hyperplanes
text: Title: Separating Measures by Hyperplanes José Correa , Svenja M. Griesbach , Elfarouk Harb , Felix Hommelsheim , Reda Jlibene , Vasilis Livanos , Eilon Solan Comments: 58 pages, 5 figures Subjects: Computational Geometry (cs.CG) ; Metric Geometry (math.MG) Given red and blue points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, connect every red point to every blue point and weigh each segment by its length under a fixed norm. What fraction of the total weight can always be captured by a single affine hyperplane separating the segments' endpoints? We study this question for finite point configurations in affine general position and, more generally, for pairs of probability measures. For dimension one, we show that choosing the best of three thresholds determined by the means of the two distributions captures at least one third of the total red-blue distance. We also give a matching upper bound. Embedding the line construction to higher dimensions shows that the guarantee of $1/3$ cannot be improved for arbitrary measures. Thus, we pivot to the family of measures whose atoms are in affine general position and whose non-atomic part places zero mass on all hyperplanes. Crucially, we establish that the worst-case guarantee is identical for finite configurations in affine general position and several natural classes of probability measures, thereby unifying the discrete and continuous formulations of the problem. For this family of measures and for higher dimensions, we extend our guarantee of $1/3$ for all norms. Our proofs combine the ham-sandwich theorem with a novel coupling argument and, in the planar case, an integral representation of norms. We also show that the optimal guarantee improves as the dimension grows, giving a lower bound of $1/2-\operatorname{O}\left(1/\sqrt{d}\right)$ as well as an asymptotically matching upper bound of $1/2$ for every $d$. For the Euclidean distance, we refine the lower bounds to $8/(8+5\pi)$ and $1/2-\operatorname{O}\left(1/d\right)$ and, for $d=2$, the upper bound to $5/11$. We also derive dimension-dependent guarantees for finite point configurations, including perfect separation of $n$ points of each color when $d\geq2n-1$.

title: OMCDE: Opposition-based Multi-Stage Matrix-Based Competitive Differential Evolution
text: Title: OMCDE: Opposition-based Multi-Stage Matrix-Based Competitive Differential Evolution Mohammad Sarhangzadeh , Shahryar Rahnamayan , Doruk Oner Comments: 7 pages, 1 figures. Published in the 2026 IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC), IEEE WCCI 2026 Journal-ref: 2026 IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC), IEEE World Congress on Computational Intelligence (WCCI), IEEE, 2026 Subjects: Neural and Evolutionary Computing (cs.NE) Differential Evolution has proven to be an effective algorithm for continuous global optimization, but it's modern high-performing variants often introduce additional complexity and computational cost. We propose OMCDE, a matrix-based competitive Differential Evolution algorithm that aims to improve optimization performance while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed approach integrates competition-driven search dynamics, adaptive behavior between optimization stages, and opposition-based initialization within a parallelizable framework. Empirical results on widely used CEC 2017 functions show that OMCDE achieves strong performance compared to several state-of-the-art DE algorithms, while remaining efficient and scalable. These findings indicate that OMCDE is a promising alternative for solving complex numerical optimization problems.

title: FIND: Frequency Invariance Disentanglement for Test-Time Adaptation in LiDAR 3D Detection
text: Title: FIND: Frequency Invariance Disentanglement for Test-Time Adaptation in LiDAR 3D Detection Dongxiao Li , Zixuan Hu , Ling-Yu Duan Comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) LiDAR-based 3D Object Detection (L3OD) is a fundamental 3D perception task, yet its performance is often compromised by domain shifts arising from diverse sensor configurations and environmental conditions. Existing Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) methods primarily leverage self-supervision in the spatial domain, yet they frequently confound semantic content with domain style due to the sparse, non-Euclidean nature of point clouds. To overcome this limitation, we propose FIND (Frequency INvariance Disentanglement), a novel TTA framework that precisely disentangles domain-invariant content from domain-specific interference within the frequency domain. Our methodology utilizes B-Spline fitting to construct locally adaptive filters integrated into a dual-stream architecture: an Invariant Stream extracts robust features to guide pseudo-labeling, while a Specific Stream enforces consistency against domain perturbations. By combining invariance-driven alignment with stability-guided regularization, our approach dynamically extracts robust domain-invariant features while suppressing domain-specific interference. Extensive experiments on cross-dataset adaptation and robust corruption benchmarks demonstrate that FIND significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code is publicly available at this https URL .

title: A structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method for variable-density incompressible flow with a partitioned time integrator
text: Title: A structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method for variable-density incompressible flow with a partitioned time integrator Zonghao Bai , Yinhua Xia , Yan Xu Subjects: Numerical Analysis (math.NA) Preserving density bounds and mass conservation, together with a conservative momentum discretization and exact incompressibility, is a central challenge in high-order simulations of variable-density incompressible flow. We develop a structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method that couples conservative density transport with an \(H(\mathrm{div})\)-conforming mixed discretization of the momentum equation. The method uses a partitioned time integrator: density is advanced explicitly by strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta stages with a bound-preserving limiter, while momentum is updated by a linearly implicit backward differentiation formula. The transport velocities are extrapolated from previously computed mixed velocities. Because the discrete solenoidal space is linear, this extrapolation preserves elementwise zero divergence and single-valued normal traces, providing compatible transport velocities without an auxiliary reconstruction or projection. For source-free transport on triangular meshes with impermeable or periodic boundaries, we prove bounds for density cell averages and limiter control-point values under the stated spatial, quadrature, and stagewise Courant--Friedrichs--Lewy conditions. The conservative fluxes and mean-preserving limiter yield global mass conservation. Numerical experiments on triangular and structured rectangular meshes demonstrate the expected convergence rates, machine-level divergence errors, and bound preservation, including in a low-density regime with high density ratio.

title: PaB-tree: Parallel B+-tree with Batch Updates
text: Title: PaB-tree: Parallel B+-tree with Batch Updates Ziyang Men , Yan Gu , Yihan Sun , Helen Xu Subjects: Data Structures and Algorithms (cs.DS) ; Databases (cs.DB); Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing (cs.DC) The B+-tree is a ubiquitous search index due to its provable I/O (cache) efficiency. Yet unlike batch-parallel binary search trees, which are both fast and widely available, no batch-parallel B+-tree offers strong empirical performance together with provable, near-optimal I/O efficiency. Prior B+-tree-based designs are either parallel but purely theoretical, with no high-performance implementation, or concurrent indexes such as the Bw-tree and Masstree, which run an order of magnitude slower on batch updates. We present PaB-tree, the first batch-parallel B+-tree with guarantees on work, span, and cache complexity alongside strong practical performance. Its core challenge -- repairing node overflows and underflows without eroding the tree's I/O advantage -- is resolved by one simple invariant: a repair never touches a sibling and is always pushed to the parent. A Promote primitive reduces batch construction and insertion to repeated node promotion, and batch deletion to reinsertion. Batch updates take O(B log_B n) work and O(log_B n) I/O per element, matching the sequential B+-tree bounds, with polylogarithmic span. Against highly-optimized parallel and concurrent baselines, PaB-tree delivers the best overall performance trade-off: up to 1.4x faster on construction and up to 3.6x faster on batch insertion than the strongest baseline, while preserving B+-tree query efficiency.

title: TOFS: Feature Selection with Swap Supervision for Semantic Communication over Fading Channels
text: Title: TOFS: Feature Selection with Swap Supervision for Semantic Communication over Fading Channels Zhiyi Zhu , Eiji Takimoto , Patrick Finnerty , Chikara Ohta Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) Task-oriented semantic communication transmits task-relevant features to support receiver inference under limited communication resources and adverse channel conditions. For image classification, the usefulness of a feature depends on the other transmitted features and the distortion introduced by the wireless channel. Effective feature prioritization should therefore account for classification performance after transmission of the selected features. This paper proposes a Task-Oriented Feature Selection (\textit{TOFS}) framework and method, which evaluates feature replacements using receiver classification loss. Loss differences confirmed under independent transmission samples provide pairwise ranking supervision for a selector network. The trained selector predicts priorities in a single forward pass. CIFAR-10 simulations demonstrate improved classification accuracy over an importance-based feature selection baseline at the same transmitted feature count and average transmit power. The proposed \textit{TOFS} framework shows 84\% accuracy performance under Rayleigh fading and Gaussian noise, compared with the 68\% performance of a SOTA method.

title: Construction of DAE solver Rodas4PW and numerical test examples with Rosenbrock and W-methods in OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl
text: Title: Construction of DAE solver Rodas4PW and numerical test examples with Rosenbrock and W-methods in OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl Gerd Steinebach Comments: 16 pages, 4 figures Subjects: Numerical Analysis (math.NA) This paper compares various Rosenbrock and Rosenbrock W-methods. To achieve this, some methods implemented in the Julia package this http URL are selected and benchmarked using test examples. The test examples include stiff ODE problems as well as differential-algebraic equations. In addition to the already known methods, the new W-method Rodas4PW is introduced and included in the tests.

title: SIFR: Stable Signed Flow Reinforcement
text: Title: SIFR: Stable Signed Flow Reinforcement Runlong Liao , Xingqian Xu , Lizhang Chen , Baiyu Su , Yufan Huang , Zhonghao Wang , Akash Gokul , Ming-Yu Liu , Qiang Liu , Yogesh Balaji Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Reward-based fine-tuning of flow models requires effectively promoting high-reward and suppressing low-reward samples, while maintaining training stability over many rounds of iterative updates. Iterative reward fine-tuning provides a simple starting point, but the positive reward weights give no explicit unfitting signal, and repeated reweighting concentrates the distribution and causes collapse. We propose Stable Signed Flow Reinforcement (SIFR), which replaces the reward weights by signed advantages to supply the missing unfitting signal, and constrains the velocity drift from a reference model to stabilize the updates, with a Lagrange multiplier that adapts the regularization strength to a prescribed drift budget. We further show that existing flow RL methods fall within this framework: they implicitly minimize the signed loss, differing in their regularization choices. We validate SIFR on SD3.5 Medium (2.5B) and FLUX.2 Klein (9B) and scale it to Cosmos 3 Super Text2Image (64B): across all 12 backbone--reward pairs with preference and rule-based rewards, it matches or exceeds existing methods, reaches their peak rewards much faster, and keeps improving over long training where they plateau or collapse.

title: TailDART: Compute-Efficient Foundation Models for Financial Time-Series Forecasting
text: Title: TailDART: Compute-Efficient Foundation Models for Financial Time-Series Forecasting Chiang Qin Zhi , Ranjan Satapathy , Erik Cambria , Joyjit Chattoraj Subjects: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) ; Computational Engineering, Finance, and Science (cs.CE) Although time-series foundation models (TSFMs) achieve strong zero-shot transferability across high-information-density physical systems, applying overparameterized TSFMs to quantitative finance is fundamentally constrained by low signal-to-noise ratios, non-stationarity, and prohibitive autoregressive decoding latency. To reconcile representation learning with institutional operational constraints, this study presents TailDART, a dense 2.68 million-parameter foundation model engineered for financial time-series forecasting. By integrating grouped-query attention into a lightweight backbone, the architecture drastically reduces Key-Value cache memory bandwidth overhead, achieving major inference acceleration (up to 48.1%) over prevailing state-of-the-art TSFMs to enable low-latency, high-throughput streaming execution. Furthermore, multi-asset benchmarks across varying temporal resolutions show that a compact model can remain competitive for market forecasting: TailDART matches the predictive fidelity of substantially larger baselines while demonstrating superior error resilience in high-volatility regimes.

title: Analyzing Code Provenance in LLMs for Programming Education
text: Title: Analyzing Code Provenance in LLMs for Programming Education Subhankar Maity , Faiza Belbachir , Omar Boucelma , Guilherme Medeiros Machado Subjects: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) ; Software Engineering (cs.SE) Large language models (LLMs) play an increasing role in programming education, challenging traditional assessment methods as they can generate fully functional code instantly. This disrupts the reliability of student submissions as indicators of learning and effort. To address this issue, code provenance is essential for tracing the origins of code and distinguishing student-authored, AI-generated, and externally sourced components. We extend the Min-K% probability approach by incorporating synthetic non-member code generation and apply it to Python code for membership inference and provenance tracking. Evaluations cover free LLMs such as GPT-2, DistilGPT-2, and DialoGPT, as well as state-of-the-art commercial models including GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, Mistral, DeepSeek, and LLaMA 3.3. Before evaluating our approach on higher-education student assignments, we validate its feasibility using Stack Overflow data. The results show that free models enable more sensitive code memorization detection than commercial models. By systematically comparing these LLMs, we assess trade-offs between detection accuracy and privacy protection, taking an initial step toward effective assessment of AI-assisted programming education through combined provenance detection and process visibility.

title: A Taxonomy-Driven Synthetic Dataset for Retrieval Effectiveness and Fairness Evaluation in Hiring
text: Title: A Taxonomy-Driven Synthetic Dataset for Retrieval Effectiveness and Fairness Evaluation in Hiring Warren Jouanneau , Morgane Hoffmann , Emma Jouffroy , Marc Palyart Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Computation and Language (cs.CL); Computers and Society (cs.CY); Information Retrieval (cs.IR) While machine learning hiring tools are ubiquitous, the need for privacy regulations and commercial sensitivity makes public benchmarking legally complex. We address this challenge by introducing a taxonomy-driven, fully synthetic HR dataset and benchmark to simultaneously evaluate retrieval effectiveness and algorithmic fairness. Grounded in 660K real freelancer profiles, our multilingual corpus features candidate profiles, project briefs, and counterfactual demographic twins. Auditing state-of-the-art embedding models reveals performance divergence from general MTEB scores, alongside fairness disparities in grammatically gendered languages. This demonstrates that general benchmarks are insufficient for HR, requiring tailored evaluations to identify Pareto-optimal models that balance semantic accuracy and fairness.

title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
text: Title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test Prahladh Harsha , Swastik Kopparty , Mrinal Kumar , Ramprasad Saptharishi , Madhu Sudan Comments: Abstract shortened due to arxiv requirements Subjects: Computational Complexity (cs.CC) ; Information Theory (cs.IT) We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an $m$-variate function $f$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial. The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if $f$ has at least $\epsilon$ expected local agreement with a degree-$k$ univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact $f$ is non-trivially close to some degree-$k$ $m$-variate polynomial even as $\epsilon$ approaches $0$ (provided $q$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$ and $1/\epsilon$). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small this http URL this paper we explore the bivariate case ($m=2$). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{F}_q^2 \to \mathbb{F}_q$ and a set of lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ of size nearly $q^{3/2}$ such that on every line in $\mathcal{L}$, $f$ has agreement $\approx 1/2$ on average with some univariate polynomial of degree $k=\sqrt{q}/2$ and yet $f$ is $1 - O(q^{-1/2})$ far from every polynomial of degree $O(k)$. On the positive side, we show that once the field size $q$ is at least $k^2/(\epsilon)^{O(1)}$ such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size $O(q/\epsilon^{O(1)})$ on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis. On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.

title: Enhanced Informed Dynamic BP Decoding Scheduling Strategies for 5G NR LDPC Codes
text: Title: Enhanced Informed Dynamic BP Decoding Scheduling Strategies for 5G NR LDPC Codes Tofar C.-Y. Chang , I-Hsiang Lee , Pin-Han Wang , Jian-Jia Weng , Yu T. Su Comments: 7 pages, 5 figures, 2022 IEEE 96th Vehicular Technology Conference Subjects: Information Theory (cs.IT) We present an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) strategy to avoid propagations of unreliable messages in the residual belief-propagation (RBP) algorithm for decoding low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. To reduce the resource needed for updating the degree-one variable nodes (VNs) in an RBP-based algorithm for decoding 5G New Radio (NR) LDPC codes, we further introduce a process consisting of several simple procedures for managing the resource consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that our RBP algorithm based on the Proposed IDS strategy outperforms existing RBP-based algorithms at the early decoding iterations. By using our degree-one VN resource managing approach, the performance of both the proposed and the existing decoders is significantly improved in decoding the 5G NR codes.

title: Controlled Excitation for Identification of Nonlinear Systems with Saturated Outputs
text: Title: Controlled Excitation for Identification of Nonlinear Systems with Saturated Outputs Adel Malik Annabi (McTAO, LJAD), Jean-Baptiste Pomet (McTAO), Dario Prandi (L2S, CNRS), Ludovic Sacchelli (McTAO) Subjects: Systems and Control (eess.SY) ; Optimization and Control (math.OC) We consider nonlinear systems whose measured output is the product of an unknown matrix and a known saturation function of the unmeasured state. Generating excitation that allows the matrix to be recovered from the output is challenging when the dynamics are largely unknown. We exploit saturation to construct this excitation. Under a geometric accessibility condition, we derive explicit open-loop controls that drive the state into regions where the saturation takes prescribed values. For componentwise saturations, this condition holds generically with as few as two independent control directions. The controls require no state measurement and only partial knowledge of the dynamics, with no information on the structure of its nonlinear part. The resulting regressor is known in advance, and the unknown matrix is recovered exactly by a closed-form regression. Under stronger structural assumptions and with sufficiently many independent outputs, an output feedback tracks prescribed reference trajectories within the unsaturated region to arbitrary accuracy and permits exact state recovery. Suitably chosen references then also enable exact identification of linearly parameterized (nonlinear) dynamics. We analyze robustness to measurement noise and illustrate the method numerically in the presence of both measurement and dynamical noise.

title: RoleWalk: training-free structural embeddings for directed graphs that transfer across graphs
text: Title: RoleWalk: training-free structural embeddings for directed graphs that transfer across graphs Maixent Chenebaux Comments: 14 pages, 3 figures. Complete technical report (20 pages) as an ancillary file. Code: this https URL (pip install rolewalk) Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Social and Information Networks (cs.SI) Structural role embeddings describe a node by its position in a graph - hub, bridge, periphery, member of a dense core - rather than by who its neighbours are. Existing methods either learn coordinates specific to one graph (struc2vec, Role2Vec, RESD) or read scales and normalisations from the whole graph (GraphWave, Digraphwave), so the same neighbourhood can receive different coordinates in two graphs; few read edge directions. We present RoleWalk, a training-free embedding that follows a short lazy random walk from each node and records, at each step, two distributions: that of the transition probabilities, through its characteristic function at a fixed grid of frequencies, and that of the walker's distance to its starting node. On directed graphs, walks that go forward then backward add who shares a node's targets or sources. The embedding depends only on a node's neighbourhood within a fixed radius, so its coordinates mean the same thing in every graph. We show that, without curvature, it is the kernel mean embedding of the walk's footprint, that it separates graphs that the Weisfeiler-Leman test cannot, and that pruning small probabilities comes with a per-node error certificate. Empirically, RoleWalk is competitive with the best role embeddings on five classification benchmarks at a fraction of their cost, has the highest scores on real directed roles in Wikipedia adminship, exceeds the published accuracy of Digraphwave at every noise level of its own Enron network-alignment benchmark, transfers centrality predictors to graphs four times larger better than existing inductive embeddings, hand-made features and a trained GIN, and embeds a million nodes in 20 s to 3 min on one CPU core. The code is open source (BSD license): this https URL

title: Bootstrap Your Own AV-Proxies: Adaptive Contrastive and Prototype Learning for Audio-Visual Segmentation
text: Title: Bootstrap Your Own AV-Proxies: Adaptive Contrastive and Prototype Learning for Audio-Visual Segmentation Junbo Zhang , Hang Su , Zhaofan Li , Hang Dong , Chao Sun Comments: Accepted to CVPR 2026 Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Audio-Visual Segmentation (AVS) aims to accurately segment sounding objects in video frames by leveraging audio-visual correspondence cues. However, it remains challenging due to the intrinsic semantic incompleteness within a single modality and the semantic gap between audio and visual representations. Traditional feature-fusion decoding approaches struggle to suppress fusion noise effectively, while recent methods that incorporate data-dependent priors often increase the complexity of modeling audio-visual correlations, leading to poor cross-domain generalization. To address these issues, we propose a novel adaptive contrastive and prototype learning framework, BYOAVP, for AVS. Specifically, we design a Self-Supervised Audio Enhancement (SSAE) module that introduces contrastive learning to adaptively align audio representations with gradient-blocked visual embeddings, thus narrowing the semantic gap between modalities. Furthermore, a Dynamic Prototype Constraint (DPC) module is developed to refine pixel-wise category perception via momentum-based prototype updating, while enhancing localization of sounding regions through cross-modal interaction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves SOTA performance across two AVS benchmarks and six sub-tasks, exhibiting strong robustness and generalization ability.

title: Large Language Model Consensus and Corpus-Adaptive Topic Modeling for Classifying and Mapping Patent Innovation
text: Title: Large Language Model Consensus and Corpus-Adaptive Topic Modeling for Classifying and Mapping Patent Innovation Sercan Ozcan , Enes Ozgozler , C. Okan Sakar Subjects: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) ; Information Retrieval (cs.IR) Patent analytics increasingly relies on transformer representations and large language models (LLMs), yet linking conceptual classification, topic formation and interpretation requires explicit decisions about model roles and the evidence retained at each stage. In this design-oriented study, we propose and demonstrate a patent analytics pipeline that links these tasks and keeps each decision open to audit. Three LLMs separately classify each patent by novelty (radical or incremental) and innovation type (product, process, service). Radical and innovation-type labels each require two supporting votes, with Incremental used as the fallback novelty label. Topics are discovered by clustering PatentSBERTa embeddings, with parameter ranges scaled to corpus size. A patent-specific stopword list is applied only when topics are represented with class-based term frequency--inverse document frequency (c-TF-IDF), and a second embedding model supports inter-topic similarity, hierarchical refinement and visualization. An LLM then labels each topic from its ranked keywords and representative patents. We demonstrate the pipeline on 30,964 public-sector-related patents retrieved from this http URL . Across five category corpora ranging from 591 to 29,215 patents, the pipeline produced 74 category-specific topic instances with a macro-average document coverage of 98.1% and topic diversity of 0.900--1.000, and fewer than 1% of classification outputs returned UNKNOWN. Because every model vote and the evidence behind each topic label are retained, analysts can audit and revise the outputs. The demonstration establishes the feasibility and traceability of the pipeline; testing its labels against expert coding and benchmarking it against alternative pipelines are identified as the next steps. The pipeline offers a reusable basis for LLM-assisted patent analysis in technology intelligence.

title: InstantHMR : Real-Time Human Mesh Recovery on Your Phone
text: Title: InstantHMR : Real-Time Human Mesh Recovery on Your Phone Mohamed Adjel , Kahina Chalabi (LAAS-GEPETTO), Vincent Bonnet (LAAS-GEPETTO) Subjects: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV) Real-time 3D human mesh recovery from a single image on mobile devices is a challenging problem with many applications, including robotics, biomechanics, AR/VR, and exergames. Current state-of-the-art models are either too slow to run efficiently on mobile devices or sacrifice accuracy for speed. We present InstantHMR, a family of open-source single-image regressors suited for mobile inference, based on the Momentum Human Rig (MHR) parametric model and trained exclusively on publicly available annotations from the SAM 3D Body dataset. Our approach achieves remarkable performance on a Samsung Galaxy S23 NPU, recovering a 6,890-vertex body mesh in 5.5 ms per person, and 0.98 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 4070 GPU. This speed surpasses all existing methods we evaluated. On mobile, it is 12x faster than the single mobile-compatible method that slightly outperforms ours in accuracy, while achieving competitive accuracy with 40.0 mm PA-MPJPE on 3DPW, 48.8 mm on EMDB and 41.7 mm on RICH. To ensure fair comparisons, we re-evaluate 11 state-of-the-art methods under a unified protocol aligned with the closest MHR-based competitors, including Meta's official MHR-to-SMPL conversion, and report their reproduction results. Additionally, we measure latency across eight different targets, ranging from desktop TensorRT to two phone NPUs. Code and models are available at this https URL .

title: Calibrated concept profiles: making the reading of a model's neurons a measurement
text: Title: Calibrated concept profiles: making the reading of a model's neurons a measurement Piotr Wilam Comments: 25 pages, 5 figures, 11 tables. Dataset: AtlasOpenCoder, tag v1, doi: https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/11472 . Code: this https URL Subjects: Computation and Language (cs.CL) ; Machine Learning (cs.LG) Interpretability has largely moved from reading a model's neurons directly to reading a second model trained on the first: a probe, a sparse autoencoder, a crosscoder. The move answered real faults -- mixed meanings, thresholds without a unit, readings that did not transfer from one study to the next -- but gave up what a direct reading alone provides: nothing trained in between, the neurons themselves named, and a reading that can be repeated and compared. Here the direct reading is made a measurement. A neuron's activation varies with the prompt, so its reading is a distribution over a population of stimuli. We declare that population: every factor around a target construct is drawn at its rate in a reference corpus and logged. From the declared distribution we generate a battery of prompts, and draw it twice. From the battery we compute the calibrated concept profile, one number per neuron, stated in units of the neuron's own spread on ordinary input; the two draws give every number a noise unit. Before the profile is read, a fixed set of checks licenses the battery on the model, and the smallest change the profile can resolve across training checkpoints is measured. Realised for Python on OpenCoder-1.5B and followed across checkpoints spanning two trillion training tokens, the profile gives what the alternatives do not report: a unit on every number, a chance level for every comparison, and which neurons carry a construct at every checkpoint. The battery, the code and the data behind every result are released.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Option Shielding
text: Title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Option Shielding Gian Luca Ascari , Isidoro Tamassia , Ying Jiao , Luc De Raedt , Giuseppe Marra Comments: Accepted at the NEmo workshop @ NeurIPS 2026 Subjects: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) ; Machine Learning (cs.LG) Shielding is a safe reinforcement learning technique that provides safety guarantees while learning, by blocking unsafe actions. Traditional shielding relies on a complete model of the environment to provide long-term guarantees. Probabilistic logic shielding (PLS) lifts the requirement of having such model, but only considers safety in the short term, typically looking only one or few steps ahead. We propose Probabilistic Option Shielding (POS), which extends PLS to the option level, recovering long-horizon safety without reintroducing the need for a complete environment model. POS learns a model-free critic directly from one-step PLS signals, to estimate the probability that an entire option will complete safely under uncertainty. We evaluate POS on safe navigation tasks in the LogiCity environment, and show that it achieves considerably safer training while matching the task performance of standard step-level PLS and other safety related reinforcement learning baselines.

title: SAS: Scene-Annotated AudioSet Strong for Joint Scene-Event Analysis
text: Title: SAS: Scene-Annotated AudioSet Strong for Joint Scene-Event Analysis Michel Olvera (S2A, LTCI, IDS), Paraskevas Stamatiadis (S2A, LTCI, IDS), Romain Serizel (MULTISPEECH), Slim Essid (IDS, S2A, LTCI), Gaël Richard (S2A, IDS) Journal-ref: Proceedings of the 11th Workshop on Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE 2026), Oct 2026, Boston, MA, United States, United States Subjects: Sound (cs.SD) Context is central to human auditory perception, as listeners interpret sounds within their acoustic environment to resolve ambiguity. However, large-scale datasets that jointly capture sound events and acoustic scenes remain limited. We address this by augmenting AudioSet Strong with clip-level scene annotations under two taxonomies for joint sceneevent modeling. A corpus-scale analysis shows that scene identity is better captured by events distinctive to a scene than by those that merely occur frequently. Reweighting event co-occurrences toward scene-specific associations produces representations that better align with human-derived taxonomies, while also exposing scenes where the acoustic and semantic views diverge. This geometric divergence predicts classification errors, while supervised validation confirms that the proposed scene annotations provide meaningful complementary information for developing scalable context-aware machine listening systems.

title: Structure and Lineage Evidence for Vietnamese Statutory Article Retrieval on DRiLL
text: Title: Structure and Lineage Evidence for Vietnamese Statutory Article Retrieval on DRiLL Duc-Vu Nguyen , Ngan Luu-Thuy Nguyen Comments: Accepted at SOICT 2026 Subjects: Information Retrieval (cs.IR) ; Computation and Language (cs.CL) We study Vietnamese statutory Article retrieval on DRiLL using features for provision identity and local form, same-law support, and citation and lineage evidence. Across five random seeds, selectors sharing candidates, listwise Qwen evidence, and learner settings improve official $F_2$ from 71.77% to 72.91%, with the largest descriptive gain on two-Article questions. Added features account for 18.20% of the proposed selector's total decision-tree split gain, measured as training-objective reduction, mainly from same-law and citation evidence. Cases reveal base provisions and amendments, companion recovery, distractor removal, and failures. These findings motivate research on other datasets, representations, and learners without establishing individual feature effects or requiring LightGBM, hand-crafted scores, or explicit graphs.

title: Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces
text: Title: Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces Yongxin Liu , Junliang Lv , Ning Wang , Yi Wang Comments: 29 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables Subjects: Numerical Analysis (math.NA) ; Analysis of PDEs (math.AP) This paper studies direct scattering by periodic fluid--solid interfaces and interface reconstruction from multifrequency near-field data. Using Helmholtz decomposition and quasi-periodic single-layer potentials, we formulate a coupled boundary integral system with the standard stress traction, establish its equivalence to the original fluid--solid transmission problem under suitable assumptions, and construct a corresponding Nyström discretization. For near-field observations at finitely many measurement points, we establish local Fréchet differentiability of the observation map with a quadratic remainder estimate. In the smooth setting, the derivative transmission problem and its boundary integral formulation are used to compute the observation Jacobian required for interface reconstruction. The interface is reconstructed by regularized Gauss--Newton iteration in a Fourier space that is progressively enriched as the frequency increases. Numerical experiments assess direct-solver accuracy and reconstruction performance for different interfaces, material configurations, and noise levels.

title: Copies Are Not Confirmations: How News Duplication Fools LLM Judges and Continual Learners
text: Title: Copies Are Not Confirmations: How News Duplication Fools LLM Judges and Continual Learners Abdelkader Metales , Miriam Grabenheinrich , Aicha Metales Comments: 19 pages, 13 tables. Code, labels and results: this https URL Subjects: Machine Learning (cs.LG) ; Computation and Language (cs.CL) Many news reports of a claim are copies of one source: wire stories, content shared within a media group, syndicated features and press releases. We ask whether LLM judges and continual learners treat such copies as independent confirmations.
